title: Teen found in shallow California vineyard grave identified nearly 50 years later as family warns killer
summary: Michelle Louise Collier vanished from Fresno in 1978 at age 15. Forensic genetic genealogy finally identified her remains found in a Kern County vineyard.
story: Michelle Collier's family speaks publicly after DNA identified the California teen nearly 50 years after she disappeared and was found buried in a vineyard. Credit: Kern County Sheriff's Office

A teenage girl whose body was found buried in a shallow grave beneath a California vineyard nearly half a century ago has finally been identified, reopening a murder mystery that had gone cold for 48 years.
Michelle Louise Collier was just 15 years old when she disappeared from Fresno in February 1978.

Four months later, a tractor operator cultivating a grape vineyard near Arvin uncovered her skeletal remains buried in a shallow grave, but investigators could not identify the teen, leaving her known only as "Arvin Jane Doe" for nearly five decades.
Her older sister, Cynthia Dunbar, said the family spent nearly 50 years wondering what happened before finally learning Michelle had been the unidentified homicide victim all along.
GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE
A school portrait of Michelle Collier, who was identified nearly 50 years after she was found slain in a California vineyard. (Kern County Sheriff's Office)

"She disappeared 48 years ago, and it was only recently that we knew where she was," Dunbar said during an emotional news conference Wednesday. "At least with this information, my family has some closure."
Dunbar also delivered a searing message to the person responsible for her sister’s death.
MICHIGAN ATHLETE LURED BY SNAPCHAT MESSAGE BEFORE BEING SHOT, DUMPED IN LAKE WHILE STILL ALIVE
Michelle Collier's family speaks during a Kern County Sheriff's Office news conference announcing her identification. (Kern County Sheriff's Office)
"The shock of finding out we lost our sister to a homicide is overwhelming to our entire family, especially our 85-year-old mother, Maria," she said.

"To the person who killed our sister, your cowardice act affected our entire family," Dunbar continued. "But make no mistake, law enforcement will find you and hold you accountable. Whether you are already incarcerated or dead, you will be found. May God bless your soul because you're going to hell if you're not there already."
Authorities said Collier’s remains were discovered June 21, 1978, near South Wheeler Ridge Road after the tractor operator unearthed the shallow grave.
DNA CRACKS 40-YEAR COLD CASE MYSTERY WITH ARREST IN LIBRARY WORKER’S SAVAGE SLAYING: POLICE
A vineyard near Arvin, California, where Michelle Collier's remains were discovered in a shallow grave in 1978. (Kern County Sheriff's Office)
An autopsy at the time determined the manner of death was homicide, although the exact cause of death could not be determined. Investigators knew they were dealing with a homicide victim.
"Without an identity for the victim, the case went cold," Kern County homicide Det. Ashley Thompson said. "For 48 years, detectives knew her only as Jane Doe."
Kern County Sheriff Donny Youngblood said generations of investigators continued revisiting the mystery, including several people who were present at Wednesday’s announcement.
"Several detectives have looked and worked on this case since 1978," Youngblood said. "These cases are outstanding to us when we come to a resolution, especially for the family members."
The remains were buried at Arvin Cemetery in November 1978 after investigators were unable to identify them through fingerprints, dental X-rays or other forensic methods available at the time.
The case was reopened multiple times over the following decades as forensic science advanced.
TIPSTER CHARGED WITH MURDER AFTER POLICE SAY ANONYMOUS CALL HELPED SOLVE 30-YEAR DISAPPEARANCE
A school photograph of Michelle Collier before the California teen disappeared in 1978. (Kern County Sheriff's Office)

Investigators got another chance in 2007 when the remains were removed from a cemetery so a DNA sample could finally be collected. The sample was submitted to the California Department of Justice, but without matching DNA from relatives, detectives were still unable to identify the teenage victim.
A forensic anthropologist examined the remains in 2008 and concluded the victim was likely between 15 and 24 years old, with evidence pointing toward the younger end of that range.

Detectives also partnered with the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, which produced a facial reconstruction of the victim and circulated her image publicly. Investigators reviewed fingerprints, dental records and missing person cases from California and Oregon, but no new leads emerged.

The breakthrough finally came in 2025 when investigators turned to forensic investigative genetic genealogy, a technique that combines advanced DNA analysis with traditional genealogical research to identify unknown victims.
Working with Texas-based forensic laboratory Othram, investigators developed a comprehensive DNA profile from Collier’s remains and identified potential relatives through genetic genealogy.
Collier’s identification marks the 86th publicly announced California case in which investigators used Othram’s forensic genetic genealogy technology to identify previously unknown human remains.
Detectives then contacted members of Collier’s family and obtained a DNA swab to compare with her mother.
In October 2025, the comparison confirmed that the unidentified homicide victim was Maria Collier’s daughter, 15-year-old Michelle Louise Collier.
Dunbar said DNA previously submitted to a genealogy database by Collier’s half-brother, sister-in-law and cousin helped investigators identify her.
COVERT DNA SAMPLE FROM COLORADO MAN'S TRASH REVIVES 44-YEAR-OLD TEXAS MURDER CASE: REPORT
Michelle Collier's family said they finally have answers after the 15-year-old homicide victim was identified nearly 50 years after her disappearance. (Kern County Sheriff's Office)

After investigators confirmed her identity, Collier's remains were removed from Arvin Cemetery in April 2026 and returned to her family, allowing them to finally bring the 15-year-old home and give her a proper burial.
"You didn’t deserve to die this way, Shelley," Dunbar said, using the family’s nickname for Michelle. "Barely 15 years old, still a child, with your whole life ahead of you.
"I’m sorry that we didn’t protect you, but you’re with Daddy now in heaven, just as you always wanted," she added. "We love you, Shelley."
While Collier’s identification marks the biggest break in the case since 1978, investigators stressed that the homicide investigation is entering a new chapter, not ending.
"Identifying Michelle is an important step, but the circumstances surrounding her death remain unknown," Thompson said.
Authorities said no suspect information was available for public release, but Thompson said identifying the victim fundamentally changes the investigation.

"Now we get to investigate it knowing who the victim is," Thompson said.

The Kern County Sheriff’s Office is asking anyone who knew Collier or has information about her life, disappearance or death to contact Detective Thompson at 661-861-3110 or the Secret Witness line at 661-322-4040.

title: ICE seeks nearly $500K fine against immigration lawyer accused of filing fake asylum claims
summary: ICE alleges attorney Suraj Raj Singh filed 118 fraudulent documents across 54 immigration cases with nearly identical claims of persecution.
story: Acting ICE Director Todd Lyons revealed that Homeland Security Investigations officers uncovered potentially thousands of fraudulent foreign workers.

EXCLUSIVE – U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is seeking more than $470,000 in civil fines against a New York immigration attorney accused of filing fraudulent documents in support of asylum claims on behalf of dozens of clients, alleging he submitted more than 100 documents containing nearly identical accounts of persecution.

Homeland Security Investigations announced it had issued a notice of intent to fine attorney Suraj Raj Singh, whose nationwide practice primarily represents Indian nationals seeking asylum before immigration courts, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
ICE alleges Singh prepared and filed 118 fraudulent documents in 54 immigration cases.
The agency is seeking the maximum permissible fine — $470,584.
TRUMP PUTS ASYLUM LAWYERS ‘ON NOTICE’ WITH NEW FRONT IN WAR ON FRAUD
Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Washington D.C., Jan. 5, 2023. (Celal Gunes/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images)

According to DHS, asylum declarations submitted in support of Singh's clients' applications were "identical or nearly identical in language and substance," containing the same or substantially similar factual narratives and supporting details describing alleged persecution.

"Fraudulent asylum claims threaten the safety of the American people, undermine our immigration system and delay the removal of dangerous criminal illegal aliens," DHS General Counsel James Percival said.

"ICE is seeking a fine of more than $470,000 from attorney Suraj Raj Singh. Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, we will hold attorneys like this accountable and put an end to the practice of defrauding and abusing our immigration system."
A notice of intent to fine is a proposed civil enforcement action that allows the recipient an opportunity to respond before any penalty becomes final.
DHS ISSUES $84B IN FINES TO ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS UNDER TRUMP ADMINISTRATION

A U.S. Department Of Homeland Security and U.S. Customs and Border Protection sign is displayed at the U.S. Customs and Border Protection Headquarters May 18, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)

The action is the latest step in the Trump administration's effort to crack down on alleged asylum fraud. In May, Percival directed DHS attorneys to pursue additional enforcement actions targeting fraudulent asylum claims.

DHS said the Singh case marks the second time the department has sought civil penalties against an immigration attorney under 8 U.S.C. § 1324c(d), which authorizes fines for immigration-related document fraud.
ICE seeks a $470,584 fine against attorney Suraj Raj Singh, alleging he filed 118 fraudulent documents across 54 asylum cases using nearly identical claims. (iStock)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Last month, ICE issued five notices of intent to fine against attorney Vinod Doddamani, seeking a combined $255,232 in civil penalties over alleged immigration document fraud.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Singh for comment.
Preston Mizell is a writer with Fox News Digital covering breaking news.

title: Escaped inmate's bid for freedom comes to crashing end after coordinated manhunt closes in
summary: Video shows deputies finding Chase Orput shirtless on railroad tracks after a citizen tip and Sparks police drone led to his capture in Nevada.
story: Video released by the Washoe County Sheriff's Office captures deputies locating Chase Orput after an alert citizen helped lead officers to his location. Credit: Washoe County Sheriff's Office
An escaped Nevada inmate's short-lived taste of freedom came to an abrupt end after a multi-agency search zeroed in on him with help from a helpful tipster, authorities said.
Video released by the Washoe County Sheriff's Office shows deputies finding 23-year-old Chase Orput lying shirtless on railroad tracks moments before taking the escaped inmate back into custody.

Authorities said he was last seen heading southwest while wearing a black-and-white striped inmate uniform, prompting an overnight search involving the Washoe County and Storey County sheriff's offices.

Authorities said a citizen from a nearby business recognized Orput near Interstate 80 and alerted the Sparks Police Department, whose drone helped direct officers and deputies to his location near mile marker 21.
'AMERICA'S MOST WANTED' FUGITIVE CAPTURED ON SAILBOAT OFF NJ COAST AFTER 20 YEARS ON THE RUN
Chase Orput was recaptured after walking away from a Washoe County Sheriff's Office inmate work crew. (Washoe County Sheriff's Office)
Orput was evaluated by medical personnel at the scene before being transported back to the Washoe County Detention Facility, where he is expected to face additional escape charges.

The Washoe County Sheriff's Office said Orput was located around 1 p.m. Tuesday, roughly 24 hours after he walked away from a Washoe County Sheriff's Office inmate work crew at about 1:30 p.m. Monday.

Authorities said the citizen's call gave officers a crucial lead, allowing Sparks police officers and Washoe County sheriff's deputies to quickly narrow in on Orput's location. Sparks police also deployed a drone to provide aerial support as deputies closed in.
CALIFORNIA DEPUTIES USE MAGNET-EQUIPPED DRONE TO DISARM KNIFE-WIELDING SEX OFFENDER HIDDEN IN GARAGE
Video released by the Washoe County Sheriff's Office shows Chase Orput lying shirtless on railroad tracks before deputies took him into custody. (Washoe County Sheriff's Office)

title: Violent anti-ICE rioter who targeted police finally faces reckoning in federal court
summary: A 42-year-old Los Angeles man was sentenced to 37 months in federal prison for targeting law enforcement during violent anti-ICE protests on a highway overpass.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

A California man accused of taking part in a violent confrontation during last year's anti-ICE riots in Los Angeles was sentenced to more than three years in federal prison after admitting he targeted law enforcement officers caught in the chaos.

Ismael Vega, 42, of Los Angeles' Westlake neighborhood was sentenced Monday to 37 months in prison and ordered to pay $253,415 in restitution for his role in the June 8, 2025, attack, the Justice Department announced.

"Those who attack our brave officers protecting public safety will face federal prison time for their crimes," U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli wrote Monday on X after the sentencing. "Let this be a warning to others who think they can act without consequences."
Vega pleaded guilty in April to obstructing, impeding and interfering with law enforcement during civil disorder.
FBI ARRESTS PROTESTER WHO THREATENED TO KILL ICE OFFICER'S FAMILY AT NJ DETENTION CENTER PROTEST, BLANCHE SAYS
According to court documents, Vega was among a large crowd gathered on the Main Street overpass above U.S. Highway 101 as protests over federal immigration enforcement descended into violence.

Prosecutors said Vega knew California Highway Patrol officers were trapped beneath the overpass when rioters began dropping burning debris, fireworks and other objects toward a California Highway Patrol (CHP) patrol vehicle parked below.
FORMER MARINE GETS 100 YEARS IN PRISON AS JUDGE CALLS ICE DETENTION CENTER AMBUSH 'AN ASSAULT ON DEMOCRACY'
Federal prosecutors identified Ismael Vega as one of the people involved in the June 2025 anti-ICE riot on the Main Street overpass in downtown Los Angeles. (The United States Department of Justice)

Court records show Vega repeatedly helped others ignite debris before setting a large piece of cardboard on fire himself. He then held the burning cardboard over the railing, lined it up with the hood of the CHP vehicle and dropped it onto the cruiser.
As the cardboard burned, Yachua Mauricio Flores, 23, poured a liquid onto the flames, causing the fire to grow as Vega stood nearby and gestured toward the blaze, according to prosecutors.

Vega also admitted throwing multiple rocks at officers as they attempted to clear the overpass. He acknowledged that the burning debris and other objects created a substantial risk of death or serious bodily injury to the officers below.
VIDEO SHOWS MOMENT CHICAGO MAN ALLEGEDLY USED SUV AS WEAPON AGAINST ICE AGENT, PROSECUTORS SAY

Federal prosecutors say people on the Main Street overpass ignited debris that was later dropped toward California Highway Patrol officers during anti-ICE riots in downtown Los Angeles June 8, 2025. (The United States Department of Justice)
"This civil disorder stood apart in its magnitude," federal prosecutors wrote in a sentencing memorandum.
Prosecutors cited a statement from a CHP sergeant with nearly three decades in law enforcement who described the impact the attack had on him and his son.
"His experience underscores how violent this incident became and the deep toll it took on all law enforcement present," prosecutors wrote.
The attack unfolded two days after violence erupted against federal agents carrying out immigration enforcement operations in Los Angeles.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS LOST OR ABANDONED HUNDREDS OF LAWSUITS AGAINST ANTI-ICE PROTESTERS, MIGRANTS: REPORT

People gather along the Main Street overpass overlooking U.S. Highway 101 as a California Highway Patrol vehicle burns below during anti-ICE riots in Los Angeles. Federal prosecutors say burning debris and rocks were dropped from the overpass toward officers beneath it. (The United States Department of Justice)
Federal prosecutors previously charged seven people in the overpass attack.
According to court documents, Vega, Flores and Adam Charles Palermo, 40, helped drop burning debris toward the CHP vehicle while others threw rocks at officers trying to clear the overpass.
Vega is the fifth person sentenced in the case.

Flores is scheduled to be sentenced Aug. 3 and faces up to five years in federal prison.

Palermo, whom prosecutors identified as the lead person charged in the case, is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. 14 after pleading guilty to assaulting, resisting and impeding people assisting federal officers with a deadly or dangerous weapon. He faces up to 20 years in prison.

title: ICE arrests more than 900 suspected human traffickers during FIFA World Cup, rescues 180 victims: DHS
summary: DHS says more than 900 suspected human traffickers were arrested and 180 victims rescued during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, including 30 children.
story: FBI Director Kash Patel highlights the successful security operations for the World Cup, Milan Olympics and F1 races, achieving zero major security incidents. Patel credits President Trump's leadership in establishing protocols and deploying over 5,000 personnel.

Federal agents arrested more than 900 suspected human traffickers and rescued 180 victims — including 30 children — during the 2026 FIFA World Cup, the Department of Homeland Security announced Wednesday.

The 905 arrests came during operations led by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement's Homeland Security Investigations, working alongside the DHS Center for Countering Human Trafficking and federal, state and local law enforcement agencies, DHS said.

"While Americans and international visitors were enjoying the FIFA World Cup, the men and women of ICE law enforcement were hard at work cracking down on human trafficking operations in FIFA host cities across the country," DHS Assistant Secretary Lauren Bis said in a statement.
"Federal law enforcement arrested more than 900 suspects and rescued nearly 200 victims. Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, we are dismantling human trafficking networks."
ELEVEN INDICTED IN ALLEGED TEXAS SMUGGLING SCHEME THAT LEFT 7 MIGRANTS DEAD IN SHIPPING CONTAINER

Fans gather before the FIFA World Cup 2026 final match between Spain and Argentina at New Jersey Stadium, also known as MetLife Stadium, in East Rutherford, N.J., on July 19, 2026. (Anadolu via Getty Images)

One of the biggest cases unfolded Friday in Dallas, where HSI agents arrested eight people accused of running an adult bookstore that investigators said had secretly operated as a brothel for more than 20 years.

The investigation began in 2023 and found that thousands of adults and children were allegedly sold for sex through the business, according to DHS. Investigators identified dozens of victims. One victim was murdered in 2024, and a defendant in that case was later convicted and sentenced to life in prison.
An Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent stands before a large American flag. (Charly Triballeau/AFP via Getty Images, File)

The eight suspects face charges that include conspiracy to commit sex trafficking, sex trafficking by force, fraud and coercion and money laundering conspiracy. The case is being prosecuted by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas.
FBI BOSS KASH PATEL DETAILS HOW AGENCY AND PARTNERS SECURED RECORD-SHATTERING FIFA WORLD CUP

In another case, HSI agents in San Francisco, working with the FBI and local police, rescued two girls believed to be victims of human trafficking. One of them had been missing from Bakersfield, California, since November 2025, according to DHS.
Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents at work. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images, File)

The trafficking cases were part of a broader security effort during the World Cup.

DHS also said its agencies seized more than 700 unauthorized drones, inspected more than 19,000 vehicles headed to stadiums and fan festivals and confiscated hundreds of thousands of counterfeit World Cup merchandise items worth more than $33 million.

title: Seattle police chief snaps over Chicago home questions, absence from city after mass shooting
summary: Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes was in Dallas when the Bite of Seattle mass shooting killed three, sparking scrutiny over his frequent travel.
story: Seattle Police Chief Shon Barnes snapped at a reporter who questioned how often he is in the city, telling him "those reports are wrong" before a staffer stepped in to hold him back. (Credit: Fox 13 Seattle)

title: 'Son of Sam' Berkowitz doesn't 'trust the media' 50 years after terrorizing city with letters to newspaper
summary: David Berkowitz says he no longer trusts the media 50 years after his first killing, declining interviews and calling himself the "Son of Hope."
story: Jonathan Fahey, former DHS deputy assistant secretary, weighs in on anti-ICE protests in Brooklyn that blocked hospital entrances, condemning NYC Mayor Mamdani's reaction. These controversial bills raise serious public safety concerns statewide.

"Son of Sam" David Berkowitz, New York's infamous .44-caliber killer who taunted the public with letters to the legendary columnist Jimmy Breslin, says he no longer trusts the media 50 years after kicking off his killing spree.
Berkowitz's first victim, 18-year-old Donna Lauria, was shot and killed while getting out of an Oldsmobile in the Bronx on July 29, 1976.
Through an intermediary, "Lighter Side of True Crime" podcaster Keith Rovere, Berkowitz declined an interview request for this story.
UNEARTHED 'SON OF SAM' PRISON TAPES REVEAL CHILLING DETAILS ABOUT SERIAL KILLER DAVID BERKOWITZ
Police mugshot showing the front view and profile of convicted New York City serial killer David Berkowitz, known as the "Son of Sam." (Hulton Archive/Getty Images)

"I don't trust the media," he wrote to Rovere in a letter shared with Fox News Digital. "They will twist and distort whatever I say. Even recently they twisted my words concerning some changes in New York's parole law which, in this instant, had nothing to do with me."
New York lawmakers are mulling over bills that would create an elder parole system and abolish life without parole.

"They riled up a victim with a false information and a distortion, thus creating the victim needless grief and pain, and more," he wrote. "This was not the first time. If the media wishes to know what I've been doing with my life, all they have to do is visit the website which has probably over a thousand pages of my prison writings and various videos, interviews and more, which viewers could easily access. Ariseandshine.org."

Police officers escort American accused (and ultimately convicted) serial killer David Berkowitz (left), known as the Son of Sam, into the 84th precinct station, New York, New York, Aug. 10, 1977. (Robert R. McElroy/Getty Images)
NEW YORK BILLS COULD ABOLISH LIFE WITHOUT PAROLE FOR SERIAL KILLERS AND COP KILLERS, CRITICS WARN

In May, Berkowitz skipped a parole hearing and wrote in a letter to the New York Post that he wasn't trying to get out. "The only place I’m looking forward to going, is to heaven to be with the Lord," the outlet quoted him as writing.
The Post asked "Son of Sam" survivor Robert Violante, 68, for a reaction.
"I sincerely doubt he is going to heaven," he said. "He is lucky he is not already in hell."
FAMILY OF SHOOTING SURVIVOR SAYS 'DEFAMATORY' TRUE-CRIME DOC PAINTED OLYMPIC EQUESTRIAN SHOOTER AS REAL VICTIM
Donna Lauria, first victim of David Berkowitz. (NY Daily News Archive via Getty Images)
Violante survived a gunshot wound to the head on July 31, 1977. His date, 20-year-old Stacy Moskowitz, did not. She was Berkowitz's final victim.
That was a year and two days after the first murder — Lauria's.
Her friend and the car's owner, 19-year-old Jody Valenti, was wounded but survived.

New York City saw a cool night, with lows in the 60s, after clouds and rain rolled in to break up scorching temperatures from the day before, according to Almanac.com. The Mets lost in extra innings to the Pittsburgh Pirates, 2-1. The Yankees had a day off after toppling the Boston Red Sox, 6-4.
LUIGI MANGIONE'S EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE DEFENSE MAY HAVE HUGE IMPACT IN HIS OTHER CASE: LAWYER

A police officer leans over in the front seat of Robert Violante's car on service road of Shore Parkway across the street from a park between Bay 14th and 16th streets in Brooklyn. Violante and his date, Stacy Moskowitz, both 20, became the 12th and 13th victims of the "Son of Sam" as they sat in a car at 2:35 a.m. Moskowitz later died from her injuries. Violante lost an eye but survived. (Dan Godfrey/NY Daily News Archive via Getty Images)

The shooting would become known as the first of what police initially called the .44-caliber killings. They terrified New Yorkers for a year. Young couples shied away from sitting in parked cars. Young women cut and dyed their hair, believing that the killer was targeting people with long, dark locks.
Valenti provided a crucial description of her attacker — a White male in his 30s with curly dark hair.

Marielena Maddalena studies a sketch of "Son of Sam" at Sheepshead photo store in Brooklyn. (Charles Frattini/NY Daily News Archive via Getty Images)
Still, it took months before police pieced together a pattern now known as the "Son of Sam" murders, when ballistic evidence linked the same gun to the July shooting and four more.
At that point, it was March 8, 1977, and Berkowitz had killed three and injured four.

In the lead-up to the one-year mark, he sent a note to the former New York columnist Jimmy Breslin, whom he had been taunting with letters signed, "Son of Sam."

"Tell me, Jim, what will you have for July Twenty-Ninth?" he wrote to Breslin, according to one of his 1977 Daily News columns. "You can forget about me if you like because I don’t care for publicity. However, you must not forget Donna Lauria and you cannot let the people forget her, either. She was a very sweet girl but Sam’s a thirsty lad and he won’t let me stop killing until he gets his fill of blood."

This note was found by police in the 1970 Ford Galaxy owned by David Berkowitz when they arrested him, late Aug. 10, 1977, as he sat in the car in front of his Yonkers, New York, home. It is written in the style of the .44 caliber killer. (Getty Images)
He went on to warn that while he'd been quiet, he hadn't been inactive.
"I am still here," he wrote. "Like a spirit roaming in the night. Thirsty, hungry, seldom stopping to rest; anxious to please Sam. I love my work."

Berkowitz's letters showed the killer was following news coverage of the case, mocked police and cemented the "Son of Sam" moniker in place of the .44-caliber killer.

"I believe Berkowitz was focused on revenge, jealousy and attention, along with the feeling of power," said John Kelly, a criminal profiler and the president of STALK Inc. "He felt he was unlovable and acted out his rage on couples who could share a romantic emotional moment. Something he felt he could never have."

Still crying in rage, Danny Carrique leaves court in Brooklyn, New York, with his friend, Neysa Moskowitz, the mother of David Berkowitz murder victim, Stacy Moskowitz, on May 23, 1978. (Dan Jacino / New York Daily News via Getty Images)

Though the night of July 29 came and went without a new victim, another shooting two days later proved key to Berkowitz's arrest. Investigators, looking for suspicious vehicles in the area, found a parking ticket issued nearby. That led police to his door in Yonkers. He was arrested on Aug. 10, 1977.
By then, the shootings had killed six and injured seven.

When searching his house, detectives found evidence that he had been closely following other crimes as well.

According to an FBI publication from July 1980, Berkowitz kept notes on hundreds of fires near New York City in the years before his arrest. Police found handwritten notes about 1,411 incidents, with details including the weather, street name and firefighters' response.

"He's one of the few serial killers that I know that I believe has completely changed his ways," said Rovere, a former prison pastor and the host of the "Lighter Side of True Crime" podcast who has been trading letters with Berkowitz for years.

Serving a life prison sentence, Berkowitz now claims to be a born-again Christian and calls himself the "Son of Hope." His letters are now signed "Bro[ther] David" or, occasionally, with his full name. Most are typed, no longer handwritten.
He spends some of his time producing illustrated religious pamphlets and posts content on his website and working on his prison ministry.

LINDSAY CLANCY’S EX-HUSBAND DETAILS ‘BIG SPIRAL’ AS EXPERT SAYS ONE PART ‘SCARED ME’ IN MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
"What happened?" he recalled asking her.
"I tried to kill myself," she responded, according to Patrick.
He then asked, "Where are the kids?"
"They’re in the basement," Lindsay told him.
Patrick testified that she did not say the children were injured, in danger or needed help.
Once first responders arrived at the Duxbury, Massachusetts, home, Patrick said he immediately ran into the basement, where he found Cora, 5, face down with an exercise band around her neck.
He removed the band before seeing 8-month-old Callan nearby in the same position with another band around his neck.
WATCH: Lindsay Clancy breaks down as jury hears husband's frantic 911 call
Patrick then searched the basement bathroom and the area surrounding a couch before finding 3-year-old Dawson inside Patrick’s home office.
"I knew he was gone," Patrick testified.
Dawson also had an exercise band around his neck. Patrick said he removed it and moved back and forth among the children, attempting CPR before first responders took over.
Jurors were later shown the clothing the children were wearing that night, along with the yellow, black and blue exercise bands recovered with them.
Before the evidence was presented, Judge William Sullivan warned jurors that some testimony and exhibits could produce an emotional reaction.

"You must not be influenced in any way by the unpleasant nature of some of the evidence," Sullivan said, reminding jurors that their verdict must not be based on "sympathy, anger, passion or prejudice or pity."

Patrick Clancy exits Plymouth Superior Court, Plymouth, Mass., Monday, July27, 2026. His ex-wife, Lindsay Clancy, is on trial for the murder of their three children. (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
Patrick’s testimony gave jurors a minute-by-minute account of the night of Jan. 24, 2023, beginning with the errands prosecutors allege Lindsay arranged to get him out of the house.

Patrick said Lindsay asked him as he was leaving to make an additional stop at CVS to buy a stool softener for Cora. She had not mentioned the item in earlier text messages about picking up takeout food, according to his testimony.
Patrick estimated that CVS was about three minutes from their home.

While inside the store, Patrick called Lindsay because the shelves were largely empty and he wanted to confirm whether a generic product would work. She initially did not answer but called him back about a minute later, at approximately 5:34 p.m.
"She was pretty quiet," Patrick said. "It sounded like she was busy."
He said he remembered ending the call believing Lindsay was probably giving the children baths or doing something else with them.

Exterior view of the home of Patrick and Lindsay Clancy in Duxbury, MA on Wednesday, February 15, 2023.  Lindsay Clancy, 32, allegedly killed their three children here before attempting to take her own life on January 24 this year.  (David McGlynn for Fox News Digital)
After leaving CVS, Patrick drove about 10 minutes to the ThreeV restaurant, where Lindsay had ordered takeout under Patrick’s name and phone number.
He then returned home and placed the bags on the kitchen island.
"The house was really quiet," Patrick said.
The house was really quiet
Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague during testimony of Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband, Patrick Clancy on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. (David L. Ryan/Pool)

He called out to his family but received no response. He opened the basement door and yelled downstairs but heard nothing. Patrick then called Lindsay’s phone at approximately 6:09 p.m. before searching the second floor.
He checked the bathroom and the children’s bedrooms before reaching the primary bedroom, where the door was locked.
"That’s when I knew something was wrong," Patrick said.
He retrieved a key that had been taped behind another bedroom door and unlocked it.
"I just saw blood everywhere, and the window was open," he testified.
Patrick described a large pool of blood in the middle of the room and blood across several surfaces, including the doorknob. Wind was blowing through the open window.
He took only one or two steps inside before running downstairs and into the backyard, where he found Lindsay directly beneath the window.

The court also played the 911 call Patrick made to authorities that night. Plymouth Superior Court Judge William Sullivan previously ruled that the media and public may not record, display, reproduce or distribute Patrick Clancy’s initial 911 call.
As the call played in court, Lindsay was seen quietly sobbing, eventually burying her face in her hands as jurors heard the 911 call her then-husband made after finding their three children.

Assistant Plymouth County District Attorney Jennifer Sprague entered a bag of prescription pills that were prescribed to Lindsay Clancy into evidence during the first day of her trial. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)

Prosecutors appeared to begin chipping away at the defense’s portrayal of Lindsay Clancy as over medicated, walking jurors through nine prescription bottles that still contained many of the pills she had been given.

Patrick Clancy testified Monday that his ex-wife had been prescribed numerous psychiatric medications in the months before the deaths of their three young children. But under questioning from Assistant District Attorney Shanan Buckingham, he acknowledged that several prescriptions had only been partly used.
"So there were a lot of pills prescribed, but not a lot of pills taken. Correct?" Buckingham asked, holding up a bag of prescription medications.
"Is that comprehensive?" Patrick responded. "Of all the pills that were prescribed?"
"These are the pills that you brought into the police station," Buckingham said. "So out of these."
"Out of those, yeah," Patrick said. "It’s possible that not a lot were taken."
Buckingham also sought to distinguish between the total number of medications prescribed over several months and how many Lindsay was prescribed at one time.

Patrick estimated that she was taking three or four medications at most. Buckingham then asked whether it would surprise him to learn that Lindsay was prescribed no more than three medications at any given time and usually two.

Patrick Clancy took the stand Monday and described watching his wife fall into a "big spiral" before she allegedly strangled their three young children inside the family’s Massachusetts home. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
LINDSAY CLANCY’S HUSBAND COULD TESTIFY FOR HER AT TRIAL OVER DEATHS OF THEIR THREE CHILDREN
"It wouldn’t be terribly surprising, no," Patrick said.

Former federal prosecutor Neama Rahmani said the questioning appeared designed to prevent the defense from controlling how jurors view the cocktail of medications that Lindsay Clancy was prescribed in the months before authorities say she strangled Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, inside the family’s Duxbury home in January 2023.
Lindsay Clancy reacts as the details of her children's deaths are read in court on Monday. (Greg Derr/Pool/The Patriot Ledger)
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE

"An important part of being a good prosecutor is not just proving your case, but anticipating the defense’s arguments," Rahmani, president of West Coast Trial Lawyers, told Fox News Digital. "The prosecution wants to get out ahead of that potentially bad evidence by arguing that even though she was prescribed all these meds, she wasn't prescribed them at the same time. At most, she was prescribed two, three, maybe four medications at once and, importantly, she wasn't taking them."
WATCH: Former prosecutor explains why pill bottles may become key evidence in Lindsay Clancy trial
FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X
HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL
Rahmani said prosecutors appeared to be getting ahead of the defense’s claim that Lindsay’s changing prescriptions contributed to her alleged psychosis.
SEND US A TIP
"The last thing you want is the defense to gain control of the key piece of evidence," he said. "It can be O.J.’s glove or a bag of pills."

Defense attorney Kevin Reddington shows a list of medications prescribed to Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her children, during his opening statement in Clancy's murder trial at Plymouth Superior Court, in Plymouth, Massachusetts, U.S., July 27, 2026.
Rahmani said the next phase will likely focus on how long Lindsay took each medication, when she stopped taking it and how many drugs she was prescribed at once.
GOT A TIP?

"It’s not uncommon for psychiatrists to try different medications and stop them when they stop working," he said. "So how long was she on the Zoloft versus the Ativan versus the Seroquel? How many pills was she taking? I think the prosecution is gonna argue that Lindsay and her doctors were trying to get her better, and the fact that she wasn't on all these pills at once really shows that the defense is trying to mislead the jury."
Lindsay Clancy's murder trial is expected to last six to eight weeks, and the witness list contains more than 200 names. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)

The defense has argued that Lindsay was suffering from psychosis and was not criminally responsible when she strangled her three young children. Prosecutors, meanwhile, framed the mom of three as a calculated killer, saying that Clancy's children were "deliberately and meticulously killed."
LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST

Buckingham alleged that Clancy deliberately sent Patrick from their Duxbury home to pick up medication and takeout food, giving herself enough time to strangle each child with an exercise band before attempting to kill herself.
The defense is expected to argue Clancy lacks criminal responsibility because she suffered from postpartum psychosis and was overmedicated. (Greg Derr/The Patriot Ledger via Pool)
During opening statements, defense attorney Kevin Reddington conceded that Clancy killed the children but argued that the only meaningful dispute is what was happening inside her mind.
GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL
"She knows that she killed these children," Reddington told jurors. "The issue for consideration is what was going on in that woman’s mind."

Clancy, a former labor and delivery nurse at Massachusetts General Hospital, has pleaded not guilty to three counts each of murder and strangulation.

title: BTK killer Dennis Rader's daughter Kerri Rawson hit with domestic violence injunction: report
summary: Kerri Rawson's ex-husband alleges the BTK serial killer's daughter warned him their children would be murdered, leading to a Florida injunction.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

Kerri Rawson, the daughter of notorious "BTK" serial killer Dennis Rader and a prominent victims' advocate, has been subject to a domestic violence injunction after her ex-husband claimed she repeatedly warned that he and their children were in danger of being murdered, according to court records first reported by the New York Post.

Rawson has become a bestselling author and advocate for victims of violent crime since her father's 2005 arrest, writing and speaking publicly about growing up as the daughter of one of America's most notorious serial killers.

A Florida judge granted the injunction after Darian Rawson filed a petition describing a series of incidents that allegedly left him fearing for his safety and the safety of the former couple's two teenage children.

The order temporarily awarded Darian Rawson full custody of the children and limited Kerri Rawson's contact with them to electronic communications. She was also prohibited from going near their home or school and from having contact with the family's pets.
MARCELLUS WILEY'S WIFE CLAIMS EX-NFL STAR THREATENED TO KILL HER BEFORE FOURTH OF JULY DOMESTIC BATTERY ARREST

Kerri Rawson, daughter of convicted BTK serial killer Dennis Rader, became a bestselling author and victims' advocate after her father's 2005 arrest. (Travis Heying/Wichita Eagle/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

The petition alleged that Kerri Rawson summoned her former husband to an Altamonte Springs police station on Jan. 5, 2025, where she allegedly told him she had psychic abilities that allowed her to determine their children were in immediate danger and would be murdered that morning.

The filing further alleged Kerri Rawson warned police that people were coming to harm the family before later calling 911 and reporting that shots had been fired, several active shooters were at an apartment complex and three people were dead. Officers who responded found the family safe, according to a police report cited by the Post.
NANCY GUTHRIE SEARCH SCENE DREW YOUTUBERS, ARRESTS AND BIZARRE ROADSIDE CLAIMS, DOCS SAY
Police later located Rawson at Orlando International Airport and transported her to a hospital, where she voluntarily admitted herself, the report said.

The injunction petition said she was later taken into custody under Florida's Baker Act, which allows authorities to temporarily detain a person for a mental health examination under certain circumstances.

An incident report obtained by the Post described Rawson as "an individual known to make inaccurate and fabricated statements about incidents that did not actually occur, due to mental health issues."
INVESTIGATORS REVISIT FLORIDA SERIAL KILLER CASE AS SEARCH RESUMES FOR POSSIBLE ADDITIONAL VICTIMS
Dennis Rader, known as the BTK serial killer, was arrested in 2005 and later pleaded guilty to murdering 10 people in the Wichita, Kansas, area. (Sedgwick County Sheriff's Office via Getty Images)
The Post also reported that Darian Rawson later alleged Kerri Rawson violated the injunction by contacting him multiple times despite the no-contact order.

Dennis Rader murdered 10 people in the Wichita, Kansas, area between 1974 and 1991 while living what appeared to be a normal suburban life with his family. His nickname, BTK, stood for "bind, torture, kill." He pleaded guilty to the murders in 2005 and is serving 10 consecutive life sentences without the possibility of parole.
Dennis Rader enters court to plead guilty to 10 murders in the Wichita, Kansas, area on June 27, 2005. (Bo Rader/Wichita Eagle/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

Rawson published the memoir "A Serial Killer's Daughter" in 2019 and has appeared in documentaries and television programs discussing her father's crimes and advocating for victims of violent crime.
A representative for Rawson did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Murdered 9-year-old begged not to go on trip with dad months before he allegedly killed her, mom testifies
summary: Kali Galanis testified that Melina Frattolin begged not to travel overseas with her father before the girl's death near Lake George, New York.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.

The mother of 9-year-old Melina Frattolin testified Tuesday that her daughter did not want to travel overseas with her father months before prosecutors say he killed the girl during a summer trip to New York.

Kali Galanis told jurors in Essex County Court that her ex-partner, Luciano Frattolin, wanted to take Melina to his native Ethiopia for two weeks in January 2025. But Galanis said the trip never happened after her daughter objected.
"She didn't want to go," Galanis testified, adding that she also became increasingly uneasy about the proposed trip.
CHILD REUNITED WITH MOM AFTER TRANSGENDER DAD, PARTNER ALLEGEDLY KIDNAP ABROAD AMID GENDER SURGERY FEARS: FEDS
Melina Frattolin, 9, whose mother testified that she objected to traveling overseas with her father months before prosecutors say she was killed during a trip to New York. (New York State Police)

Galanis' testimony offered jurors a glimpse into the family's disagreements over Melina's travel arrangements and her growing concerns about Frattolin's travel plans with their daughter months before Melina's death.

Galanis said she had concerns about allowing Melina to travel internationally with Frattolin after the couple separated in 2019. She testified that her attorney warned her about cases in which estranged parents took children overseas and refused to return them.
Galanis testified that Frattolin later proposed extending the Ethiopia trip. She said conversations with Melina about the trip ultimately convinced her to cancel it.
MAN ACCUSED OF KILLING PARTNER ARRESTED IN MEXICO NEARLY TWO YEARS AFTER FLEEING WITH THEIR TWO CHILDREN

Luciano Frattolin is on trial in Essex County, New York, after pleading not guilty to one count of second-degree murder and one count of concealment of a human corpse in connection with the death of his 9-year-old daughter, Melina Frattolin. (New York State Police)
"I became uncomfortable," Galanis testified.
"I was not ok with that anymore," she said of the proposed trip.
Instead, Frattolin suggested taking Melina on a vacation through the northeastern United States, Galanis testified.
NEW HAMPSHIRE SUPREME COURT OVERTURNS ADAM MONTGOMERY'S MURDER CONVICTION IN DAUGHTER HARMONY'S DEATH
Authorities released this image of the vehicle driven by Luciano Frattolin and his daughter, Melina Frattolin, before he allegedly made a false kidnapping report. (New York State Police)
Authorities have said Frattolin and Melina traveled through Connecticut and New York before the child was scheduled to return home to Quebec.

Prosecutors allege that on the day Melina was scheduled to return home to Quebec, Frattolin falsely reported that she had been abducted by two men in a white van, prompting an Amber Alert. Investigators later determined there was no evidence she had been kidnapped, authorities said. Melina's body was later found partially submerged in shallow water near Eagle Lake in Ticonderoga.
Frattolin has pleaded not guilty to one count of second-degree murder and one count of concealment of a human corpse.

The trial also heard testimony Monday from New York State Police investigator Daniel Mauro, who said Frattolin remarked during questioning that "it would've been easier" to kill his daughter overseas, including in Italy or Ethiopia.

Mauro testified the comment came after investigators asked Frattolin whether he had any reason to harm his daughter.
Frattolin's trial is continuing in Essex County Court.

title: Charlie Kirk murder case as 'straight-forward' as it gets, prosecutors argue as case nears trial decision
summary: Utah prosecutors say alleged confessions, DNA, surveillance video and eyewitness testimony support sending Charlie Kirk murder suspect Tyler Robinson to trial on all seven counts.
story: The Charlie Kirk assassination trial hears explosive testimony as suspect Tyler Robinson's former roommate, Lance Twiggs, reveals a confession during the preliminary hearing in Provo, Utah. Twiggs, granted immunity, detailed text messages and in-person admissions where Robinson claimed responsibility for killing Kirk and wished he hadn't done it.

Utah prosecutors are turning up the heat on Tyler Robinson, the man accused of assassinating Charlie Kirk, arguing that the evidence against him easily meets the standard required to send the case to trial.

Following the five-day preliminary hearing earlier this month, prosecutors on Tuesday filed the first of three written briefs ordered by Judge Tony Graf, urging him to send Robinson's case to trial and arguing the evidence overwhelmingly establishes probable cause on every charge.

"This is likely as straight-forward a bindover decision as this Court will ever see," prosecutors wrote. "After admitting to several friends, including his roommate and romantic partner, that he assassinated Charlie Kirk at Utah Valley University (UVU) on September 10, 2025, in front of approximately 3000 eyewitnesses, Defendant surrendered to law enforcement for that crime."
The filing argues Robinson's alleged admissions are only part of the case.
FRIEND OF CHARLIE KIRK LABELS COURTROOM EVIDENCE 'DEVASTATING' AFTER CHILLING SURVEILLANCE FOOTAGE SHOWN
Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, is seen in court in his first in-person court appearance on Dec. 11, 2025. (Pool/KSL-TV)
"These admissions, along with others, establish probable cause to support most of the elements of the charges," prosecutors wrote.

"DNA testing, surveillance video, and eyewitness testimony buttress those elements and demonstrate probable cause to support the remaining elements. The Court should bind Defendant for trial over on all counts," they continued.
TYLER ROBINSON'S AND LANCE TWIGGS' DNA BOTH ALLEGEDLY FOUND ON KEY EVIDENCE IN CHARLIE KIRK'S ASSASSINATION
Alleged texts between Lance Twiggs and Tyler Robinson were shared in court. (Fox News; Rick Egan/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)
According to the filing, Robinson allegedly confessed to former roommate and romantic partner Lance Twiggs, writing, "I had the opportunity to take out Charlie Kirk, and I took it."

Prosecutors say Robinson also admitted planning the assassination for "a bit over a week," discussed trying to retrieve the rifle after the shooting and later wrote, "I'm going to turn myself in willingly."
CHARLIE KIRK JUDGE DENIES TYLER ROBINSON'S ATTEMPT TO HAVE POTENTIAL DEATH PENALTY REMOVED

Judge Tony Graf in 4th District Court in Provo on Friday, April 17, 2026, during a hearing for Tyler Robinson, accused in the fatal shooting of Charlie Kirk. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune via Pool)

The 28-page memorandum repeatedly points to evidence introduced during the preliminary hearing, including surveillance video investigators say tracked Robinson across Utah Valley University before and after the shooting, DNA recovered from the suspected murder weapon, a fired cartridge casing, a towel and screwdriver, and eyewitness testimony placing the alleged gunman on the rooftop overlooking Kirk's event.
FOLLOW US ON X
Prosecutors argue the evidence leaves little doubt that Robinson should be bound over for trial on all seven counts.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE U.S. NEWS

Charlie Kirk speaks at Utah Valley University on Sept. 10, 2025, in Orem, Utah. Kirk, founder of Turning Point USA, was speaking at his "American Comeback Tour" when he was shot in the neck and killed. (Trent Nelson/The Salt Lake Tribune/Getty Images)

Prosecutors also argue Robinson planned the assassination for more than a week, intentionally targeted Kirk and knowingly endangered numerous bystanders by firing a high-powered rifle into a crowd gathered to hear the conservative activist speak. Prosecutors argue the evidence easily clears Utah’s probable-cause standard at this stage of the case.
GET BREAKING NEWS ALERTS
Judge Graf requested written arguments after concluding the five-day preliminary hearing earlier this month rather than immediately making a ruling.
The defense is expected to file its written opposition in the coming weeks, followed by a final response from prosecutors before oral arguments are scheduled for Sept. 1.
SEND US A TIP
Robinson, 23, has not yet entered a plea. He faces aggravated murder and six additional felony and misdemeanor charges stemming from Kirk’s killing.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
If Judge Graf finds probable cause, Robinson will be bound over for trial. Prosecutors are seeking the death penalty on the aggravated murder charge.
Fox News' Lee Ross and Michael Ruiz contributed to this report.

title: Nolan Wells mystery deepens as email indicates teen drank heavily before vanishing
summary: A newly released Marine Patrol email listed 18-year-old Nolan Wells’ alcohol intake as “heavy" during the search for him after he disappeared on a boating trip to Horn Island.
story: 'Crime Stories with Nancy Grace' host Nancy Grace discusses the mysterious death of Nolan Wells, an 18-year-old found dead after a July 4th boat trip. Grace scrutinizes the investigation, pointing out the discovery of deep red subcutaneous tissue on Wells' occipital bone and the suspicious absence of his lungs and throat when the body underwent a second, independent autopsy.

The mysterious death of 18-year-old Nolan Wells has taken another turn after a newly obtained document listed the missing teen's alcohol intake as "heavy" as authorities searched for him on Horn Island over the Fourth of July weekend.
The document, a July 5 Mississippi Department of Marine Resources Marine Patrol email obtained by Fox News Digital, was sent to the U.S. Coast Guard as authorities searched for Wells.
Along with his physical description and last known location, the email lists "Alcohol intake: Heavy," but does not identify the source of that information.
Wells disappeared while on a boating trip to Horn Island with friends. An extensive multi-agency search ended July 6 when his body was discovered.
SEARCH CALLED OFF AFTER BODY MATCHING MISSING TEEN NOLAN WELLS FOUND OFF MISSISSIPPI COAST

A newly released Marine Patrol email listed 18-year-old Nolan Wells’ alcohol intake as "heavy" while authorities searched for him after he disappeared during a boating trip to Horn Island. (Christine Wonsley/Facebook)
Authorities have not publicly identified a cause or manner of death, and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's autopsy and toxicology results remain pending.
The newly reported details come days after a private autopsy commissioned by Wells' family concluded his cause and manner of death were "undetermined pending investigation."
NOLAN WELLS INDEPENDENT AUTOPSY DOESN'T POINT TO FOUL PLAY, FORMER MEDICAL EXAMINER SAYS

During a July 22 news conference, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said an area of "red discoloration" was found on the back of Wells' head but said Dr. Roger Mitchell, who performed the independent autopsy, could not determine a cause or manner of death pending further investigation.
"Crime Stories with Nancy Grace" host Nancy Grace later discussed the findings on her show, where she raised additional questions about the investigation.

She pointed to what she described as deep red tissue beneath the skin at the back of Wells' head and said the independent pathologist did not receive Wells' lungs or throat when conducting the second autopsy.
Grace also questioned whether those findings could be significant but emphasized that she did not know what caused Wells' death and noted there were "many accidental possibilities."

Nolan Wells' body was found July 6, but both the official and independent autopsies have yet to determine how he died, while questions remain about discoloration on his head. (Jackson County Sheriff's Department via Facebook)
"There is deep, red, subcutaneous tissue" on the back of Wells' head, Grace said, adding that the discoloration was localized rather than consistent with postmortem blood pooling.
"I don't know," Grace said. "There are many accidental possibilities."

The Jackson County District Attorney has defended the investigation amid growing public scrutiny, saying authorities are following standard procedures and awaiting forensic testing before drawing conclusions.
Authorities have not announced whether foul play is suspected.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Jackson County Sheriff's Office and the Mississippi State Medical Examiner's Office for comment.

title: Two Florida inmates die in rare double execution after SCOTUS denies stays
summary: The Supreme Court denied stays of execution for two Florida death row inmates, clearing the way for the state's first double execution since 1964.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Florida executed two convicted murderers Tuesday after the U.S. Supreme Court rejected their final appeals, marking the state’s first double execution since 1964.
The court denied two separate requests for stays in the planned executions.
Former police officer James Duckett, 68, had been scheduled to die at noon on Tuesday, but the execution was delayed awaiting results of the stay requests before the Supreme Court.
Duckett was executed by lethal injection and pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m., according to the Florida Department of Corrections.
THOMAS UNLOADS ON COURT FOR HELPING CONVICTED MURDERER BUT IGNORING 'LAW-ABIDING CITIZENS'
James Duckett was executed by lethal injection and pronounced dead at 1:19 p.m. on Tuesday. (Florida Department of Corrections)
Duckett was convicted of raping and murdering an 11-year-old girl in 1987.
The Supreme Court also denied a separate stay for Dominick Occhicone, an 80-year-old who was convicted of murdering his ex-girlfriend’s parents in 1986.
The Florida Department of Corrections said Occhicone's execution, also by lethal injection, was carried out at 6:13 p.m. local time.
JUDGE BLOCKS ALABAMA'S NITROGEN GAS EXECUTION METHOD, RULES IT IS UNCONSTITUTIONALLY CRUEL
Occhicone became the oldest inmate executed in Florida.
Dominick Occhicone was executed by lethal injection and pronounced dead at 6:13 p.m. on Tuesday. (Florida Department of Corrections)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Occhicone's execution marked the first time Florida executed two inmates in one day since 1964. It was just the second double execution in the U.S. this century and the first since Arkansas executed two inmates in 2017.

Florida executed 19 inmates in 2025, according to a Fox News Digital review of Florida Department of Corrections data. The 12 people the state has executed so far this year are more than double the next closest state, with Texas having executed four inmates this year, according to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice.
Clouds hover over the entrance of the Florida State Prison in Starke, Fla., Aug. 3, 2023. (AP)
Speaking Tuesday at the Florida Sheriffs Association Summer Conference, Gov. Ron DeSantis said his administration is on pace to carry out more executions than any other in Florida history.
"I think we'll probably end up having done more than any administration in the history of the state of Florida," DeSantis said.
The governor stressed he does not view the number as a point of pride.

"I'm not, like, taking pride in that because it's a weighty thing, but to me, as we move through those and bring justice, that makes a big difference for a lot of people out there who suffered really, really serious tragedies," he said.

title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Kyiv hours after Zelenskyy warns of major strike
summary: Multiple explosions rocked Kyiv after Russia launched ballistic missiles, hours after Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of a massive overnight assault.
story: Paul Gigot discusses Trump's decision to grant Ukraine a license for Patriot missile production. Seth Jones analyzes the move's impact on Ukraine's defense, current battlefield challenges and potential Russian escalation against NATO.
Russia launched a ballistic missile attack on Ukraine's capital early Thursday, with multiple explosions reported across Kyiv, according to Ukrainian officials.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged residents to seek shelter as blasts rocked the city. Reuters, citing a witness, reported hearing multiple explosions.
The Ukrainian Air Force also said Russia was targeting the capital with ballistic missiles.
RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY
An explosion lights up the sky over the city during a Russian missile and drone strike amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, July 2, 2026. (Gleb Garanich/Reuters)
Klitschko later said several non-residential sites caught fire following the strikes. There were no immediate reports of casualties.
The attack came just hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Russia appeared to be preparing a major overnight assault.

"I received a report from Air Force Commander Anatolii Kryvonozhko," Zelenskyy wrote on X Wednesday, saying Russia had prepared a "massive attack several days ago" and that there was a "high probability" it would be carried out overnight.
ZELENSKYY SAYS PUTIN 'LOST THE INITIATIVE' AS UKRAINE'S TECH INDUSTRY RESHAPES THE WAR
People take shelter inside an overcrowded metro station during a Russian missile and drone strike amid Russia's attack in Kyiv, Ukraine, July 30, 2026. (Alina Smutko/Reuters)

"It is important that our partners fully understand what is happening and that the protection of lives directly depends on their readiness, or lack thereof, to help us with air defense missiles," Zelenskyy said.
The Ukrainian president made the appeal after returning from the United States, where he met with President Donald Trump.
Trump recently announced at the NATO summit in Turkey that the United States would license Ukraine to manufacture Patriot air defense systems, according to The Associated Press.
"First and foremost, this concerns the United States and those partners that have Patriot missiles and can provide them to support our defense," Zelenskyy wrote.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with President Donald Trump at the White House during his visit to Washington, D.C., July 28, 2026.
"Every partner knows what is needed and fully understands the consequences of marking time."
Fox News Digital's Emma Bussey and Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Sudan's forgotten war leaves millions hungry as global attention remains elsewhere
summary: El Fasher and El Obeid remain flashpoints as UN reports detail war crimes, mass rape, and genocide conditions in Sudan's escalating civil war.
story: New footage shows families lining up for water as UNICEF warns children continue to bear the brunt of the war. (Video: UNICEF via AP.)
As multiple international crises grip the world, from Iran to Russia’s war in Ukraine, Sudan quietly remains one of the largest humanitarian and displacement disasters in the world.

Since the outbreak of hostilities in 2023, over 14 million people have been displaced and nearly 34 million people are in desperate need of humanitarian support, accounting for 10% of global needs, according to the International Rescue Committee.

"The war in Sudan has caused the world's largest humanitarian crisis and has escalated into a regional war involving all of its neighbors as well as numerous Middle Eastern powers," Alan Boswell, Project Director for the Horn of Africa at International Crisis Group, told Fox News Digital.
"Despite this, world leaders continue to ignore the conflict, leaving it to subordinates. That approach continues to fail," Boswell added.
COULD THIS AFRICAN NATION BECOME TRUMP'S NEXT TERROR TARGET AS JIHADISTS CLOSE IN ON POWER?

Women and children queue to receive free food being distributed in al-Mohayra camp for displaced people, near the city of El-Obeid in the southern Kordofan region, on June 29, 2026.  (AFP via Getty Images)
The United Nations says that some 19.5 million people are experiencing acute hunger, and 4.5 million people have fled the country.
The U.S. also recently imposed an additional round of sanctions against the Sudanese Armed Forces for allegedly using chemical weapons in 2024 in violations of the Chemical Weapons Convention.
The Sudanese government denied the allegations.

The Trump administration has made significant efforts in trying to mediate between Russia and Ukraine, as well as bring Israel’s war against Gaza to an end. The administration is also trying to uphold a shaky ceasefire that was agreed with Iran to halt the war that began on February 28.
"For three years, we have warned that Sudan was on the brink of catastrophe, and those warnings have gone unanswered," said International Rescue Committee Country Director Richard Data.
Sudan’s recent outbreak of civil war, following years of coups and credible accusations of ethnic cleansing and genocide, persists under the radar.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS MORE THAN $1B IN UN BUDGET CUTS AS REFORM PUSH GAINS MOMENTUM
Members of Sudanese Armed Popular Resistance Force take part in a military parade for fresh graduates, in Al-Qadarif state, in eastern Sudan on May 20, 2026.  (AFP via Getty Images)

The civil war broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese Armed Forces led by Gen. Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and Gen. Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, widely known as "Hemedti," leader of the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The two had been in an uneasy alliance ruling the country following the 2019 overthrow of Sudan’s longtime dictator, Omar al-Bashir, who had been in power since 1989. Together, the generals staged another coup in 2021, toppling the interim civilian government that had been in power after the fall of Bashir.
While both the Sudanese Armed Forces and RSF are accused of committing atrocities, recent reports have highlighted the brutality of the RSF.
A major focus of the deteriorating conditions has been in El-Obeid in North Kordofan state, where an escalating hunger crisis is plaguing over 100,000 displaced people in camps throughout the city.
"What we need to do is really now to plan for the scale-up beyond the 100,000 people that we have been supporting," said World Food Programme Sudan Country Director, Abdallah Alwardat.

Members of the Sudanese army's Special Mission Forces batallion in the Northern State hold a parade in Karima city on May 19, 2024. Sudan has been in the throes of conflict for over a year between the regular army led by de facto ruler Abdel Fattah al-Burhan and the RSF led by his former deputy Mohamed Hamdan Daglo.  (AFP via Getty Images)
El Fasher in the Darfur region is another major flashpoint, where the RSF took control in October 2025 and killed more than 6,000 people in the initial siege of the city.

A recent July report from the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights revealed widespread acts of sexual violence against women and girls, some as young as 12, including reports of mass and gang rapes committed by the RSF.
The RSF is also accused of abduction, with survivors describing incidents of girls and women being beaten, having their hands tied behind their backs, and being driven away in a Land cruiser.

Sudanese displaced people gather at the Zam Zam refugee camp outside the town of El-Fashir in the Darfour region of Sudan, during a visit by U.N. officials, on July 1, 2004. The U.N. humanitarian aid and refugee agencies appealed Wednesday, Feb. 7, 2024, for $4.1 billion in international support for embattled civilians in Sudan amid signs that some may be dying of starvation after nearly a year of war there between the forces of rival generals. (AP Photo/Karel Prinsloo, File)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The United Nations and other human rights groups have accused the RSF of perpetrating ethnically targeted attacks and concluded that at least three components of genocide have been overwhelmingly met, including deliberately inflicting conditions of life intended to destroy a group in whole or in part.

A U.N. report from September 2025 found that the Sudanese Armed Forces have also committed war crimes and attacked civilian populations and infrastructure. Both the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces targeted civilians with perceived affiliations to the enemy, executing, torturing and raping victims.

title: Antisemitic violence reaches deadliest level since 1994, new global report finds
summary: The J7 report reveals 20 people were killed in antisemitic attacks in 2025, marking the deadliest year since 1994 with a 97% rise in violence.
story: Cornell Law professor William Jacobson discusses a report finding that rising antisemitism is forcing many Jewish Americans to hide their identity on ‘America Reports.’
A shocking new report says 2025 was the deadliest year for antisemitic attacks worldwide since 1994.

The J7 Large Communities’ Task Force Against Antisemitism released its second annual report, which tracks antisemitic hatred in the seven countries outside of Israel where over 90% of Jews live. According to the report, 20 people were killed in antisemitic attacks in 2025. All of the deadly attacks took place in J7 countries.

The Anti-Defamation League (ADL) is one of two organizations representing the Jewish diaspora in the U.S. in the J7, which includes similar organizations from Australia, Canada, Argentina, the U.S., the U.K., Germany and France.
CHRISTIAN LEADERS HOLD EMERGENCY SUMMIT IN JERUSALEM TO CONFRONT GLOBAL RISE IN ANTISEMITISM
Police cordon off an area at Bondi Beach after a terrorist attack at a Hanukkah celebration in Sydney, Australia, on Dec. 14, 2025. (Mark Baker/AP Photo)
ADL Senior Director of Global Research and Diplomatic Affairs Aykan Erdemir told Fox News Digital that the report’s findings show "there’s no time to waste" in combating hate.

"This isn't a warning sign anymore, it's already happening," Erdemir said. "If governments let antisemitism take root and perpetrators walk free, the violence won't stop with Jewish communities. History shows Jews are the canary in the coal mine: when hatred against Jews rises unchecked, it's an early warning that everyone's safety and rights are at risk."

The J7 report finds that there were over 23,000 antisemitic incidents in J7 countries throughout 2025 – this represented a 97% increase in violent incidents and a 136% increase in total antisemitic incidents since 2022.
The Hamas terror attacks of Oct. 7, 2023, sent antisemitic hate skyrocketing worldwide.
GERMAN OFFICIALS WARN ISLAMIST, FAR-LEFT RHETORIC DRIVING SPIKE IN ANTISEMITIC ATTACKS

Firefighters are seen tackling a blaze at Highfield Road in the Golders Green neighborhood of London, following an arson attack on four charity ambulances belonging to the Jewish Community volunteer Ambulance Service. (PA/PA Images via Getty Images)

According to the report, each of the countries face an environment where antisemitism is "no longer confined to the fringes." Countries are witnessing anti-Zionism associated with the conflict in Gaza becoming "a vehicle for antisemitic expression" and educational institutions becoming an "acute flashpoint" for hatred. Combined with growing online extremism, Jewish people "across the globe report hiding their Jewish identity in public" and questioning "whether they have a future in their home countries."
Individually, the report shows how countries face their own unique challenges in quashing hatred.

A member of the public leaves the scene with her child, who is covered in an emergency blanket, after a terrorist attack at a Hanukkah celebration at Bondi Beach on December 14, 2025, in Sydney, Australia. Two terrorists dressed in black fired several shots at Sydney's world-famous Bondi Beach, that led to the deaths of 15 people and many others injured. (Photo by George Chan/Getty Images)

Australia, which has seen a 270% increase in antisemitic incidents since 2021, was home to the Bondi Beach terror attack in December 2025, during which 15 people were killed. The report says that both Islamist and left-wing extremist threats in the country "need to be prioritized, and dealt with effectively."

In Germany, a 215% increase in antisemitic incidents has been coupled with the highest per capita rate of incidents, with 69.8 incidents per 1,000 Jewish residents in 2025 for a total of 8,725 incidents.
Antisemitic hate on display at an anti-Israel protest in London. Antisemitism in the U.K. is hitting record levels since the Hamas terror attacks on Oct. 7. (Campaign Against Antisemitism on X)

The report said that normalization of hate "remains the most pressing challenge" in Germany, with the rise in incidents attributed to the "confluence of far-right ethno-nationalism, left-wing anti-Zionism, and Islamist extremism simultaneously."

In Canada, which has experienced a 60% rise in antisemitic incidents since 2021, there is a concern that "foreign state interference" is at play, in addition to "the exploitation of domestic institutions by extremist networks."
SIGN UP FOR ANTISEMITISM EXPOSED NEWSLETTER
Temple Emanu-El in Toronto, Canada was shot at on March 3, 2026. No injuries were reported. (Nick Lachance/Toronto Star via Getty Images)

The U.S. has had a 131% increase in antisemitic incidents since 2021. Though antisemitic incidents declined significantly from 2024, the 6,274 antisemitic incidents tracked in 2025 included 300 reports of physical assault.

France has witnessed a rise in antisemitic incidents of 124% since 2021. The report notes that there is "a growing climate of discrimination" where Jews in France report being refused service, denied contracts and excluded from events.

In the U.K., which has experienced a 64% increase in antisemitic incidents since 2021, 48% of 3,700 antisemitic incidents were motivated by anti-Zionism, and 53% included references to the conflict involving Gaza.
London, UK, Dec 9 2023, anti-Israel protesters hold a banner saying "From the river to the sea." (Andy Soloman/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images)

Though the government in Argentina is pro-Israel, the country "has generated conspiratorial antisemitic backlash from the left and from fringe nationalist movements," the report said. Since 2021, Argentina has seen a 46% increase in antisemitic incidents.

The J7 report also added a special chapter on antisemitism in Ireland, which is not a J7 country. While Ireland has only a 2,200-person Jewish community, it has reported 143 incidents of antisemitism. Despite antisemitism in Ireland taking hold "primarily in everyday settings," unlike J7 countries, Ireland has no national plan for combating antisemitism and no security funding for the Jewish population.
