title: Wife of Kansas City Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy out of ICU after allegedly being shot by their son
summary: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was in a shooting over the weekend at the couple’s Northern Virginia home.
story: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, wounded in a shooting over the weekend at the couple’s Northern Virginia home, has been moved out of intensive care, head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday.

Mia Bieniemy, 57, is improving steadily after she was shot Sunday, allegedly by the couple’s adult son at their Washington, D.C., home in the suburb of Ashburn, Reid told reporters at Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri.
The three-time Super Bowl-winning coach was going through a list of his injured Chiefs players when — without prompting — he provided an update on Mia Bieniemy’s medical condition.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
“She’s doing great. She’s doing better and great from where she was, out of the ICU unit and making progress,” Reid said.
“So, we’re happy about that. EB [Eric Bieniemy] is still with her and that part’s important that that stays in place.”

Elijah Zion Bieniemy, the couple’s 27-year-old son, was arrested and booked on suspicion of malicious wounding, use of a firearm in commission of a felony and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling, according to a Loudon County Sheriff’s Office statement.
Authorities have not yet revealed any possible motive for the shooting, only calling it a “domestic” disturbance.
Dramatic video and audio of the law enforcement response showed a chaotic scene outside the Bieniemy home early Sunday evening.

Deputies could be seen carrying the wounded Mia Bieniemy away from the home as other law enforcement agents, rifles drawn, headed toward the house on Northpark Drive where Elijah Bieniemy was arrested.
Mia Bieniemy still had the strength to call 911 herself, Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman told NBC News earlier this week.

The suspect fired a .22-caliber Ruger “causing injuries to the area of her left forearm and left shoulder with a projectile traveling across her chest,” according to a criminal complaint filed in support of Elijah Bieniemy’s arrest.
He was booked into the Loudoun County Adult Detention Center with his next court date set for Aug. 31.

Eric Bieniemy, 56, has one of the most high-profile assistant coaching jobs in pro football, running the Kansas City attack that includes future Hall of Fame quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce, the new husband of 14-time Grammy winner Taylor Swift.
It’s not known when Eric Bieniemy will be back with the Chiefs, who will open the exhibition season Aug. 15 and the regular season Sept. 14.
“We stay in touch with him, keep him abreast of everything that’s going on,” Reid said. “He’s got the [practice session] tape, watching whatever spare time he’s got there.”
A representative for the Loudoun County Public Defender, the office representing Elijah Bieniemy, could not be immediately reached for comment Wednesday.
“I can’t confirm the ICU question but I can confirm that LCSO detectives have spoken to her at the hospital,” Loudoun County sheriff’s spokesperson Leah Paul told NBC News in a statement.

title: Deodorant for kids: Derms talk the right age for deodorant and the best ones for young skin
summary: Kids are hitting puberty earlier — and needing deodorant sooner. Dermatologists share the best kids’ deodorants for sensitive skin, plus when and how kids should start using them.
story: We don’t always have the answers, but we have some people on speed dial who do — which is why we present to you our series FYI where we have experts explain if lip balm is actually bad, how often you should wash your hair and more.

It used to be that as kids approached their teen years, they’d start incorporating deodorant into their routine. But these days, lots of kids are reaching for it before they’ve even turned 10 years old. Because of this, brands have poured into the kids’ deodorant space in recent years, with gentler formulas aimed at tweens and even younger children.

Dermatologists say the shift tracks a real biological change. “This reflects the fact that many children are entering puberty earlier than previous generations,” says Dr. Kristina Collins, a board-certified dermatologist specializing in Mohs micrographic surgery, as well as surgical and cosmetic dermatology in Texas. “Body odor is often one of the first signs that the apocrine sweat glands are becoming active. If a child is experiencing body odor that affects their comfort or confidence, using a gentle deodorant can be appropriate.”

But is it safe for kids to wear deodorant? And if they’re going to, what should you look for in a formula? To get the answers to these questions, I spoke with Collins and another board-certified dermatologist.
Is deodorant safe for kids?

Deodorant is generally safe for kids to use, including during those early tween years when body odor first shows up. That said, kids’ skin tends to be more sensitive than adult skin, so the formula matters more than it might for a grown-up reaching for whatever’s under the sink.

“Heavy fragrances may trigger irritation or allergic reactions and alcohol-heavy formulas can sting or dry out the skin,” says Collins. “If your child has sensitive skin, even ingredients that are ‘natural’ can trigger allergic reactions.”
Translation: It’s worth paying closer attention to labels and doing a bit of trial and error to find something that works for your child’s skin, rather than assuming any deodorant will do.
At what age should a kid start wearing deodorant?

There’s no universal starting line for deodorant use and it really comes down to your child’s own body, not a birthday on the calendar. “It is based on when the sweat glands become active, which is different in everybody,” says Dr. Debra Jaliman, a board-certified dermatologist in New York City. “Most kids can start once body odor becomes noticeable, typically between the ages of 8 and 10.”

The easiest way to know it’s time is if you or your child start noticing a change in smell, especially after gym class, recess, or a hot day; that’s usually the signal that their apocrine sweat glands (ones located in your armpit that secrete oily sweat) have kicked in. At that point, introducing a gentle, kids’ deodorant can help with odor, comfort and confidence.
The best deodorants for kids

To come up with a list of the best deodorants for kids, I used expert guidance (find it below) to select options safe for younger skin. I also focused on trusted brands or products with at least a four-star average rating from hundreds of shoppers.
Deo Stick

I regularly use Tubby Todd products and love how gentle they are, so their Deo Stick is an easy pick for sensitive skin. It’s aluminum- and baking soda-free, using tapioca starch and magnesium hydroxide (ingredients our experts say are gentle enough for kid skin) to absorb wetness and fight odor-causing bacteria. According to the brand, it is gentle enough for kids ages 6 and up.
Level Up Boys Deodorant

Level Up Boys Deodorant is made specifically for young, sensitive skin. It has an Ocean Fresh scent and is free of aluminum, alcohol and parabens. Similar to the Tubby Todd option, it uses natural tapioca starch to absorb wetness. Reviewers note that the scent is pleasant without being overpowering, and say that it’s effective for 24 hours.
Evereden Kids Deodorant

Evereden’s deodorant has an aluminum-free formula that’s made without baking soda or silicones. It contains vitaminsE and  B5 to nourish skin and it is dermatologist-tested, according to the brand. It also has a sweet scent of rose, strawberry, and vanilla.
Hello Unicorn Deodorant

This deodorant is free of aluminum, parabens, phthalates, dyes and baking soda and contains shea butter to keep underarms soft and hydrated. It’s dermatologically tested and vegan, with a sweet watermelon and peach scent. The bright packaging is also appealing for younger kids.
Fresh Monster Kids Natural Deodorant

This deodorant delivers 24-hour odor protection without aluminum, parabens or phthalates, according to the brand. It’s hypoallergenic and dermatologist-tested for sensitive skin, glides on clear without white marks, according to parents who’ve bought it, and it comes in a playful gummy burst scent. Parents also say it helps kids who get sweaty and stinky in gym class or on the playground, and that they like that it isn’t irritating.
Want more from NBC Select? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.
How to shop for deodorant for kids

Both Collins and Jaliman recommend starting kids with deodorant rather than antiperspirant, since most children simply need help with odor rather than sweat reduction (which is what antiperspirant does — more on that below). Beyond that, they suggest looking for gentle formulas with minimal, recognizable ingredients rather than long lists of additives.

For kids with sensitive skin in particular, both dermatologists recommend opting for fragrance-free options or those with only light fragrance, since heavier scents and unnecessary extras are more likely to cause irritation on young, developing skin.
Do kids need antiperspirant?

Deodorant and antiperspirant often get lumped together, but they do different jobs. Deodorant works by masking and reducing odor, while antiperspirant actually blocks sweat production, typically using aluminum-based compounds.

“For most children, deodorant alone is sufficient because it helps reduce odor without affecting the body’s natural sweating process,” says Collins. “Antiperspirants contain aluminum salts that temporarily reduce sweating and are typically only necessary if a child has excessive sweating that interferes with daily life. If excessive sweating is present, it’s worth discussing with a pediatrician or dermatologist to determine the best treatment.”

In other words, reach for deodorant first, and don’t feel pressure to introduce antiperspirant unless your child is dealing with sweating that goes beyond the normal, everyday kind. And even then, talk to a doctor before you add aluminum and other ingredients to their body care routine.
Frequently asked questions

Not as much as the packaging might suggest. “The biggest differences are usually in the fragrance and marketing,” says Collins. “Children’s deodorants often use milder fragrances and are more likely to be formulated for sensitive skin. But from an ingredient standpoint, many are very similar to adult deodorants.”
In many cases, the kid-focused branding is less about a fundamentally different product and more about making an everyday routine feel approachable for a first-time user.

Deodorant alone isn’t the whole equation. Both Collins and Jaliman emphasize that good hygiene habits are just as important, if not more so, in keeping body odor in check. That means taking daily showers or baths, especially after sports or physical activity, and wearing clean clothes and breathable fabrics that don’t trap sweat and bacteria against the skin.
Building these habits alongside deodorant use can go a long way in helping kids feel fresh and confident as their bodies go through changes.

After receiving these products from the brand, I tested most of these Cécred products over a period of two to three months, although I’ve been using a few in my regular hair care routine for multiple months before writing this review. Here’s what I kept in mind while testing:

Texture/consistency: The texture and finish of a hair product is especially important to someone like me with fine, natural hair. I considered the slip, feel, and weight of each product, and how it felt on my hair and hands both during and after application. Versatility: I kept in mind how well the products could be used across different styles, situations and hair types. Packaging: I noted any issues or barriers to easy use posed by the packaging, or any ways in which the packaging made using the product faster or more efficient.Results: Of course, I was sure to consider how well each product lived up to its claims and whether or not I had any noticeable changes to my hair during or after using them. I was also on the lookout for how well the results held up in different environments and during my normal activities, like during workouts at the gym, eight-hour work days, humid summer nights out and even a day spent at the beach.

What is Cécred?

Cécred began in 2024 as a hair care line for “all types and textures,” whether straight, curly, coily, wavy or more. The initial launch featured the release of the Foundation Collection, which (along with its celebrity founder) helped propel the brand’s virality with the popularity of products like the Edge Restoring Drops. The brand followed up with the Protection Collection in summer 2025, and the latest release, the Styling Collection, just launched this past March.

Much of the brand’s technology focuses on replacing lost protein in your hair strands, using bioactive keratin, honest and lactobacillus ferment as the three key ingredients. The bioactive keratin, which is naturally-derived from wool protein, mimics keratin in hair for added protein, while the honey acts as a hydrating humectant and helps activate the prebiotic properties of the lactobacillus ferment for a healthy scalp biome, according to the brand.
Who is Cécred for?

In a word: anyone. One of the brand’s strengths is its versatility: the products are formulated to work well for all hair types and textures. Even if you’re not dealing with issues like brittle strands, dryness or itchiness, Cecred’s products are great for just regular maintenance of a healthy head of hair. However, if you do have any of the above struggles, it works especially well. The Hydrating Shampoo and Conditioner, along with the Oil Ritual and Moisturizing Deep Conditioner, are all great for treating damaged hair, and have all been game-changers in my own hair’s levels of hydration and strength.

You can probably find comparable versions of products like the Strong Hold Gel and the Wrap & Set Foam from other brands at lower prices. For example, I love Mielle’s Pomegranate and Honey Curl Defining Mousse ($10.99) and Got 2B’s Glue Blasting Freeze Spray ($7.99).  However, the brand’s reparative products from the Foundation and Protection collections are definite standouts based on the results they’ve given me.
Bottom line: it’s definitely worth the price, and if you’re considering trying it, my advice is to go for it full steam ahead.

How to choose a meat delivery service

The first factor you’ll want to consider is the type of meat offered. While various services specialize in specific types — for example, Omaha Steaks is known for its high-quality cuts of steak and beef — many offer a range of beef, poultry, pork and even seafood. That being said, your personal preference is most important in this case, so you’ll want to look for a service that specializes in your favorite types, or at least has a wide enough selection that you’ll be able to find the cuts you’re looking for.

According to Pierrel, two non-negotiables for raising meat are avoiding antibiotics and added hormones. Adding hormones is banned in chicken but still legal in beef, so Pierrel suggests checking for third-party verification, like the USDA Process Verified shield, which shows that a brand’s processes have been independently audited by the USDA.

She also says it’s important to understand these various certifications. “Words like ‘premium’, ‘natural,’ and ‘butcher’s cut’ have no legal definition; they just sound official,” she says. However, there are a few terms she suggests keeping an eye out for when looking at how your meat was raised.

Grass-fed and pasture-raised labels are great to look for if your budget allows it (since they tend to be a bit pricier). While grass-fed tells you what an animal ate, pasture-raised ensures the animal lived unconfined, outside of the grazing area, says Pierrel. “That combination produces meat that’s more nutrient-dense per bite, with a higher omega-3 profile, so it satisfies you with less,” she says. For an insider tip, she recommends looking for grass-finished meat as well, since it guarantees grass for life, unlike the grass-fed labeling.USDA Organic is the federally inspected certification that guarantees the meat has been fed organically, with no pesticides, antibiotics or added hormones, and real access to pastures, says Pierrel. There are pros and cons to both fresh and frozen meat, according to the experts. The choice will ultimately depend on your personal preferences and uses for the meat.

Fresh meat is great for meals you’ll be preparing right away or in the days soon after your delivery. Usually, being able to cook the meat right away will result in a better texture and flavor, says Kais. However, since it has a shorter shelf life, it needs to be enjoyed quickly. Fresh meat also ages through transit, whereas frozen meat is flash frozen right after processing, which preserves it at its peak, says Pierrel.Frozen meat is an excellent alternative to fresh, especially from a nutritional and safety standpoint. Pierrel says it’s also “the smarter way to stock up”, since you can save it for later in your freezer, while Kais adds that it often also provides more selection, since specialty cuts may not be available fresh. The only con is that frozen meats can sometimes experience changes in texture after thawing; however, Kais says that it shouldn’t be a major issue if handled properly (and in my experience, I had no issues with texture).

Beef in the US is graded by the USDA, and primarily focuses on marbling, which is the intramuscular fat that’s woven inside of the muscle, according to experts. “Marbling is important because it melts during cooking, helping keep the meat more tender and flavorful,” says Kais. However, Pierrel says that many shoppers aren’t aware of exactly how the grading is assessed. “The grade is assessed on the ribeye, between the 12th and 13th ribs, the fattiest section of the animal, and that single measurement grades the entire carcass, so every cut from that animal is sold under it,” she says. Since the grade measures taste, rather than nutrition or lifestyle conditions, leaner grass-fed and pasture-raised options may be graded lower simply for the lower fat content. Given that, she suggests looking at those kinds of meat, along with USDA Organic meat, if you’re more concerned with nutrition and animal welfare. “The best steak is the one that matches your goal,” she says.

title: St. Paul’s first female mayor under investigation after police chief’s sexual harassment complaint
summary: The city has hired an outside law firm to investigate the allegations against Mayor Kaohly Her, who has been in office for just seven months.
story: The St. Paul, Minnesota, police chief has submitted a sexual harassment complaint against the city’s first female mayor, alleging she behaved inappropriately toward him and other members of his department, the local NBC affiliate reported Wednesday.
The city has hired an outside law firm to investigate the allegations against Mayor Kaohly Her, who has been in office for just seven months.
Chief Axel Henry, who has led the St. Paul Police Department since 2022, outlined the allegations in an April 1 letter his lawyer sent to the St. Paul city attorney.
“The City is on notice that Mayor Her has engaged in illegal conduct towards City employees,” attorney Christopher Madel wrote in the letter, which was obtained by the NBC affiliate, KARE.

Henry sent the letter of complaint after having become “aware that the Mayor’s conduct has extended beyond isolated incidents and has included sexual harassment of subordinate City employees, including members of the Saint Paul Police Department,” Madel wrote.
“Chief Henry is not only seeking to address the wrongdoing but also create a measure of protection for his team, signaling that such conduct will not be tolerated,” Madel wrote.

Included with the letter is a screenshot of an alleged text message from Her to an unnamed city employee that reads “Happy Weiner Wednesday! Wish I was having a (hot dog emoji) with you all on 6 today!”
Below the text message is an internet meme showing a swaddled baby with an adult’s head, which has been redacted, The Minnesota Star Tribune reported.
“When she wraps you up in her blanket after you gave her a good weinering,” reads the caption.
“Wienering” is an internet slang term for sexual intercourse and is frequently misspelled as “weinering.”
The letter alleges that “Her has used one or more mobile phones to communicate inappropriate, and, indeed, unlawful text messages.”
But it does not spell out any other specific allegations of inappropriate communications.

Madel wrote that future litigation is “reasonably foreseeable” and demanded that the city “immediately take all steps necessary to perform a full filesystem extraction of each of Mayor Her’s mobile phones.”
In a written statement Wednesday, Her said she has cooperated with the investigation and believes the “full facts will come to light.”

“As Mayor, I take my responsibility to treat every employee with professionalism and respect very seriously. I recognize that some of my attempts at humor fell short of the standard I expect of myself,” she said.
Police spokesperson Nikki Muehlhausen said, “Chief Henry and the department has no comment at this time.”
The Star Tribune reported that Resolute Law, based in St. Cloud and described on its website as a “women-owned firm,” has been hired to investigate the allegations.
The law firm did not respond to a request for comment on the status of the investigation.
Her, 53, was born in Laos and spent part of her childhood in a refugee camp. She was 3 when she arrived in the U.S., and she grew up in Illinois and Wisconsin, according to her campaign biography.
The Star Tribune reported that she had faced an accusation of inappropriate behavior before.

Her was hit with a restraining order petition last year by a former friend who claimed she had sent her “inappropriate or sexualized questions” and had gotten her removed from the National Kidney Foundation Board.

The petition was denied by Ramsey County District Court Referee Elizabeth Clysdale, who wrote that the text messages filed showed that Her had not threatened her former friend and that Her’s husband had tried to help resolve the issue.
Clysdale also wrote there was no proof that Her had played a role in the woman’s removal from the National Kidney Foundation Board, the newspaper reported.

title: Anthony Fauci invokes Fifth Amendment right not to testify at Covid hearing
summary: In his opening statement, the former top health official accused Sen. Rand Paul of having an “unhinged obsession” with him and wanting him put “behind bars.”
story: Dr. Anthony Fauci declined to answer senators’ questions at a contentious hearing Wednesday on the origins of Covid and the government’s handling of the pandemic, saying he would invoke his Fifth Amendment right to avoid the possibility that Republicans would use his testimony to prosecute him for perjury.

The surprise decision set the stage for a hyperpartisan hearing that yielded no new revelations about the origins of the coronavirus or the government response to the pandemic. But the absence of Fauci’s testimony presented plenty of opportunities for Republicans and Democrats to put forth dueling narratives about those issues — and about Fauci himself.

Republicans on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee used their allotted time to criticize Fauci’s recommendations during the Covid pandemic, accusing Fauci, the former head of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, of providing harmful advice on issues such as lockdowns and of lacking candor about the origins of the coronavirus.

Democrats came to Fauci’s defense, painting the hearing as a Republican-led effort to entrap him into committing perjury and using their time to focus criticism on the Trump administration’s healthcare policies.

After Fauci had invoked the Fifth Amendment more than 100 times, committee Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., said as the hearing ended that he would call for a vote to hold him in contempt of Congress. He said after the hearing that the committee would vote on the issue next week.

Paul, a longtime critic of Fauci, has clashed with him numerous times at congressional hearings. Paul has accused him of lying to Congress about the issue of “gain of function” lab research on viruses, which makes them more dangerous to better understand them, and whether funding from the National Institutes of Health ultimately made its way to the Wuhan Institute of Virology in China. Fauci has previously denied the allegations.
On Tuesday, Paul answered a reporter’s question about how he would respond to people who argue that he was trying to put Fauci in a position to perjure himself.

“There’s no risk to perjury if you tell the truth,” Paul said. “In fact, he can even admit to not telling the truth in the past. He can admit destroying records. He can admit to, you know, not adequately presenting both sides of equations, which isn’t really a crime. He can admit to anything. The only thing he can’t do is lie again.”

In his opening statement, Fauci said Paul’s repeated attacks on him formed his rationale for deciding to invoke his Fifth Amendment right. Fauci cited what he characterized as Paul’s “obvious obsession with calling for my prosecution, his repeated slanderous comments about me” and his decision to publicly release Fauci’s personal journal.

“The only conclusion I can reach is that the sole reason he is calling me before this committee is to get me to say something — anything — that could vindicate his repeated public pledges that I end up, in his words — quote — ‘behind bars,’” Fauci said in his opening remarks.

“Any reasonable person who has followed his unhinged obsession with me would readily come to the same conclusion,” he continued. “Therefore, although it pains me to do so because of the respect I have for the legislative branch of government and my decadeslong record of cooperating with Congress, under the advice of my attorneys, I will invoke my right under the Fifth Amendment of the Constitution to refrain from answering your questions.”

In the final hours of his administration, former President Joe Biden issued pre-emptive pardons to Fauci and others to shield them from what Biden characterized as potential political prosecutions. This week, Paul did not preclude the possibility that Fauci could face charges over his testimony, saying “we’re going to find out” whether he should be prosecuted.

The pardon was a factor in his legal team’s determination that Fauci should not answer senators’ questions, because Republicans had consistently implied that the pardon would not apply to new statements.

During the hearing, Republican senators repeatedly tried to goad Fauci into responding to their questions — with Josh Hawley, R-Mo., at one point asking him to identify the colors of his tie and the floor’s carpeting.

Fauci answered each question, regardless of the topic, with the same line: “On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution.”
At the end of his period of questioning, Paul told Fauci that he would face “repercussions” for not answering.

“The committee will have to consider after this hearing what appropriate action should be taken against you for the failure to testify after being directed to do so,” Paul said. “It’s against the law to obstruct an investigation of Congress. There will be repercussions to your refusal to testify today.”
When Paul concluded, Fauci’s lawyer, David Schertler, tried to say something to the senators but was repeatedly cut off by Paul, who ultimately ordered security to remove him from the committee room.
Shortly after he left the hearing, Schertler told NBC News that Fauci “has a valid Fifth Amendment privilege, and he has the right to assert it.”
“That’s what I was trying to tell the committee, and that’s all I was trying to tell the committee,” he said.
In a separate statement, Schertler called Paul’s actions “outrageous.”
“It proves the baseless and vindictive nature of this proceeding and Rand Paul’s personal vendetta against Dr. Fauci,” he said.
During his time to speak, the top Democrat on the committee, Gary Peters of Michigan, criticized the Republicans’ handling of the hearing, saying he believed the hearing “does real damage.”

“It’s tempting to turn one person into the scapegoat for a crisis that hundreds of officials across both the Trump and the Biden administration were responsible for handling,” Peters said, adding that people were facing death threats.
“This is only going to, unfortunately, deter other scientific experts from public service to understand that this is what they would have to go through as they provide their advice to us,” he said.

Separately, Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., told reporters ahead of his period of questioning that he would not ask Fauci questions, arguing that the “show trial is a perjury craft for criminal prosecution going forward.”
During the hearing, Blumenthal defended Fauci and compared the Republican-led proceedings to Sen. Joseph McCarthy’s anti-communism hearings of the 1950s.

“We should not be part of a rerun of that kind of effort,” Blumenthal said. “This attempt to rebrand one of the most challenging times in our nation’s history is a shortsighted act of desperation that will leave us less prepared for the next pandemic.”

Schertler said in a statement that the circumstances surrounding Fauci’s appearance “regrettably made his continued cooperation impossible,” accusing Paul of taking “an intense and seemingly pathological course of retribution, revenge, and obsession with Dr. Fauci” that has ultimately led to Fauci and his family’s facing threats and harassment.

“Dr. Fauci devoted his lengthy career to saving millions of lives globally through scientific discovery and sound public health policy,” Schertler said in the statement. “The accusations that Chairman Paul continues to propagate are false and disgraceful, and we will examine all options to hold him accountable.”

title: Trump announces plans for sprawling Dulles Airport makeover
summary: The plans include redoing two of the concourses and removing the airport’s aging shuttles, known as “people movers.”
story: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump announced a sweeping makeover of Dulles International Airport on Wednesday, including building new concourses and removing its aging shuttles, known as “people movers.”

“We are announcing plans to add more than 5 million square feet of new or renovated space. We’ll replace the current C and D concourses, which are basic disasters, all the while preserving the iconic original terminal,” Trump said at an event in the Oval Office.
Trump said he selected the designs “after an extensive review of more than 30 proposals with the top architects anywhere in the world.”

The redone airport, in the Virginia suburbs of Washington, will include a “magnificent” multistory parking garage with 32,000 parking spaces. “It’ll be actually the largest garage in the world,” Trump said.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the “people movers,” which transport travelers through terminals, will be replaced by a faster and more efficient “horseshoe rail system.”

He added that the project’s $22 billion cost won’t need to be federally funded. It will be “bonded for $22.5 billion. United is going to partake in part of the payment, but the airlines who participate in the project are going to pay for it,” Duffy said.

United Airlines said in a news release that the work will include more than 5 million square feet of new or renovated space, with new and modernized concourses, an expanded main terminal and upgraded boarding areas and ticketing facilities.
Duffy said that there is still some permitting left to do but that officials are hopeful the project can begin by next spring.
Trump said that they hoped to have the project completed within two years and that the airlines’ projection for the work was originally 60 years.
The Transportation Department said in a news release that “the transformation will occur in phases over several years.”
United presented a different timeline in its release, saying the project will “transform the airport over the next decade into a modern, world-class gateway.”
At the White House event, Duffy said: “We’re trying to move at the speed of President Trump. It’s never fast enough, but we’re going as quickly as possible.”
At the airport, travelers’ reactions were mixed, with some telling NBC News they had no major issues with the airport — besides the people movers.

“They jam you in like sardines. You smell diesel fuel all the way back,” said Bill Eberhardt, who was waiting to pick up family members and said he flies out of the airport three or four times a year.
Becky Saleh, who’d just arrived from Paris, said the vehicles, also known as “mobile lounges,” aren’t very welcoming.
They’re “very old-fashioned,” and “they’re hot, they’re sticky,” she said, adding that it “seems like a very antiquated way of moving people in this day and age.”
As for the airport itself, Saleh said that it’s “easy in and out compared to some major airports” but that “I think there could be some improvements.”
Trump has been eyeing the project for months. His motorcade took a detour through the Northern Virginia airport in October to “assess potential future projects,” the White House said at the time.
Trump, a former real estate mogul, later said he had big plans for the airport.
“We’re gonna make that into something really spectacular. We have an amazing plan for it,” he said in December.

title: James Comey legal team argues DOJ’s seashells case erodes ‘bedrock’ principles
summary: It’s the second time the Trump administration has found a way to criminally charge the former FBI director, whom Trump has targeted for years.
story: Allowing the seashells-based prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey to move forward would erode core constitutional rights protecting free speech, Comey’s legal team told a federal judge in North Carolina on Tuesday.

On Tuesday, members of Comey’s eight-person legal team filed a motion asking a judge to toss the seashells case, saying it is “not based on a good-faith application of the law to the facts; instead, it effectuates a yearslong campaign by the President to use the criminal process to punish Mr. Comey for his protected speech and because of the President’s deep-seated animosity.”

The Trump-driven case must be cast aside “under two bedrock legal doctrines,” they said: that the case was instigated based on Comey’s protected speech and that the government engaged in selective prosecution.

“Dismissal of federal criminal charges under these doctrines has historically been rare. That is because for decades the DOJ’s independence and integrity have guarded against the use of the criminal process to punish enemies or settle political scores,” they wrote. “The prosecutions of Mr. Comey mark a sharp break from that tradition.”

Comey’s team also filed a separate motion Tuesday seeking the disclosure of grand jury records in the case, arguing that while “grand jury proceedings are typically entitled to a presumption of regularity, the irregularities surrounding the return of the indictment in this case overcome that presumption.”

Comey’s team had already argued Monday that the seashells case should be tossed because Comey’s Instagram post was not a true threat, arguing that “dictionaries, context, precedent, and common sense” gut the Trump administration’s claims about the meaning of the numbers “8647.”

A Justice Department official who was not authorized to discuss the case previously told NBC News that the case was a “complete loser” and a “waste of resources” and predicted that it would be tossed before trial. “No reasonable person could believe that Comey intended to threaten the president via seashells,” the person said. “Everyone at this DOJ should be ashamed. I know I am.”
U.S. District Judge Louise Flanagan is overseeing the case. If the case survives to trial, Comey would be arraigned Sept. 30, and the trial would take place Oct. 21 in New Bern, North Carolina.

Matthew Petracca, a rookie federal prosecutor and former Republican official in New Jersey, brought the case under the U.S. attorney for the Eastern District of North Carolina, W. Ellis Boyle, a Trump administration appointee, but he dropped off the case in late May.
In one of their motions, Comey’s lawyers note that Petracca became an actual assistant U.S. attorney on April 26, just two days before the Comey case was brought.

“We note that Mr. Petracca was at all times professional in his interaction with the defense team,” Comey’s attorneys wrote. “We only note his limited experience in that it is unusual in most circumstances for such a high-profile case to be delegated to a junior attorney.”

Petracca, they write, had a “background in state Medicaid fraud and little federal criminal experience” and has since “withdrawn from the case and transferred to the Civil Division.” Assistant U.S. Attorney Timothy Severo is now heading the prosecution.

Comey’s team made a similar argument of vindictiveness and selective prosecution after former White House aide Lindsey Halligan brought a case against him over testimony he gave in 2020. Included in that filing was a 60-page list of statements that Trump made about Comey from May 2017 to the fall of 2025.

But a judge never ruled on the arguments of vindictiveness and selective prosecution in that case, instead finding the entire case was invalid because Halligan could not legally hold the position she claimed.

title: Senate confirms Jay Clayton as new director of intelligence
summary: The Senate approved federal prosecutor Jay Clayton as the next director of national intelligence.
story: WASHINGTON — The Senate approved President Donald Trump’s choice to oversee the country’s spy agencies, with the Republican majority voting Tuesday to install top federal prosecutor Jay Clayton as the next director of national intelligence.

Clayton, the U.S. attorney for the Southern District of New York in Manhattan, will inherit a much smaller agency after his predecessors cut the office’s workforce in a series of firings in recent weeks and months. And his confirmation follows accusations from Democratic lawmakers and former national security officials that the Trump White House has tried to use the intelligence agencies to wage partisan political warfare.
The vote was 51-47 along party lines. Trump praised Clayton after the vote, writing on social media: “Jay is outstanding in every way, and will do a spectacular job as Director!”
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google

After Clayton was confirmed, Sen. Mark Warner, D-Va., the Intelligence Committee’s vice chairman, explained why he voted against the nomination in a statement and expressed hope that Clayton would not cave to possible political pressure from the White House.

“Having known and worked with Jay for years, I was encouraged when he was first nominated for the position of DNI,” Warner said. “Unfortunately, I came away from his confirmation process with serious reservations about whether he would be willing to stand up to political pressure when it matters most.”
The Republican leader of the Intelligence Committee, Tom Cotton of Arkansas, welcomed the vote in favor of Clayton.

“Jay Clayton is a highly qualified nominee with a deep experience combatting a wide range of national security threats,” Cotton said in a statement. “As U.S. attorney, Mr. Clayton has worked hand in glove with our intelligence agencies and counterterrorism personnel to lock up criminals who threaten our national security.”

Hours earlier, the acting intelligence chief, Bill Pulte, announced on social media what he called a fifth round of job cuts at the Office of the Director of National Intelligence since he took office in June. But he did not say how many positions were cut or how many employees were fired or merely reassigned to other intelligence agencies.
Pulte described the move as “an approximately 30% Staff Reduction from Weeks Ago.”

The National Intelligence Director’s Office had roughly 2,000 employees at the start of Trump’s second term last year, and his first director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, had proposed cuts in the workforce of about 40%. The 30% reduction Pulte cited could put the current workforce at about 1,000, former officials said.
The National Intelligence Director’s Office and the White House declined to comment.
A spokesperson for Warner said Pulte has failed to share with lawmakers information about workforce reductions or a rationale for the cuts.

“The Acting DNI has been quick to announce firings and make public claims about them, but has so far declined to provide the Senate Intelligence Committee with the information necessary to assess the accuracy of those statements or the basis for those decisions,” said Rachel Cohen, Warner’s communications director.

Congress created the national intelligence director’s position in the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks with the aim of ensuring that information was shared across the country’s spy agencies.
But Trump and some Republican lawmakers have called for scaling back the office, which they say has become a bloated bureaucracy.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
Clayton enjoys stronger support among Republican lawmakers than Pulte, a Trump loyalist who came to the job without relevant national security experience.

At his confirmation hearing this month, Clayton refused to say who won the 2020 election, sidestepping questions that could put him at odds with Trump. Trump has repeatedly claimed without evidence that the 2020 election, which Joe Biden won, was rigged.

Democrats on the Intelligence Committee said Clayton’s answers raised doubts about whether he would provide accurate information to Trump if it was out of line with his views or whether he would protect spy agencies from possible political manipulation.
Trump picked Pulte to succeed Gabbard after she said she was resigning because of her husband’s cancer diagnosis.
Pulte won Trump’s approval as head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, where he launched investigations into Trump’s perceived political enemies.

title: Washington says goodbye to Sen. Lindsey Graham, a ‘true American original’
summary: A special ceremony at the Capitol and a funeral service at the National Cathedral were held Tuesday. A second service is planned for Wednesday in Graham’s native South Carolina.
story: WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump, congressional colleagues and world leaders Tuesday said their final goodbyes to Sen. Lindsey Graham, the influential and colorful foreign policy hawk whose sudden death this month at age 71 stunned Washington and reverberated in capitals around the globe.

Eulogizing Graham, R-S.C., at his funeral service at Washington National Cathedral, Trump called him “a respected statesman, a giant of the United States Senate and a true American original who left us much too soon.”

“Lindsey rose from a small town in rural South Carolina, a place he loved so much, to become a constant fixture of American politics at the highest level and a force to be reckoned with all over the world,” Trump told those gathered. “For more than 30 years, nothing of consequence happened in this capital without Lindsey Graham knowing about it. Nothing of significance happened anywhere in the world without Lindsey Graham having a view on it, and no bill became law in the most exceptional republic in human history without Lindsey Graham having a say in it.”

Graham had been a vocal critic of Trump’s when they ran against each other in the 2016 presidential race. But Graham became one of Trump’s closest and most trusted allies on Capitol Hill and a frequent golf partner.

title: Wife of Kansas City Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy out of ICU after allegedly being shot by their son
summary: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy was in a shooting over the weekend at the couple’s Northern Virginia home.
story: The wife of Kansas City Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy, wounded in a shooting over the weekend at the couple’s Northern Virginia home, has been moved out of intensive care, head coach Andy Reid said Wednesday.

Mia Bieniemy, 57, is improving steadily after she was shot Sunday, allegedly by the couple’s adult son at their Washington, D.C., home in the suburb of Ashburn, Reid told reporters at Chiefs training camp in St. Joseph, Missouri.
The three-time Super Bowl-winning coach was going through a list of his injured Chiefs players when — without prompting — he provided an update on Mia Bieniemy’s medical condition.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
“She’s doing great. She’s doing better and great from where she was, out of the ICU unit and making progress,” Reid said.
“So, we’re happy about that. EB [Eric Bieniemy] is still with her and that part’s important that that stays in place.”

Elijah Zion Bieniemy, the couple’s 27-year-old son, was arrested and booked on suspicion of malicious wounding, use of a firearm in commission of a felony and discharge of a firearm inside a dwelling, according to a Loudon County Sheriff’s Office statement.
Authorities have not yet revealed any possible motive for the shooting, only calling it a “domestic” disturbance.
Dramatic video and audio of the law enforcement response showed a chaotic scene outside the Bieniemy home early Sunday evening.

Deputies could be seen carrying the wounded Mia Bieniemy away from the home as other law enforcement agents, rifles drawn, headed toward the house on Northpark Drive where Elijah Bieniemy was arrested.
Mia Bieniemy still had the strength to call 911 herself, Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman told NBC News earlier this week.

The suspect fired a .22-caliber Ruger “causing injuries to the area of her left forearm and left shoulder with a projectile traveling across her chest,” according to a criminal complaint filed in support of Elijah Bieniemy’s arrest.
He was booked into the Loudoun County Adult Detention Center with his next court date set for Aug. 31.

Eric Bieniemy, 56, has one of the most high-profile assistant coaching jobs in pro football, running the Kansas City attack that includes future Hall of Fame quarterback Patrick Mahomes and tight end Travis Kelce, the new husband of 14-time Grammy winner Taylor Swift.
It’s not known when Eric Bieniemy will be back with the Chiefs, who will open the exhibition season Aug. 15 and the regular season Sept. 14.
“We stay in touch with him, keep him abreast of everything that’s going on,” Reid said. “He’s got the [practice session] tape, watching whatever spare time he’s got there.”
A representative for the Loudoun County Public Defender, the office representing Elijah Bieniemy, could not be immediately reached for comment Wednesday.
“I can’t confirm the ICU question but I can confirm that LCSO detectives have spoken to her at the hospital,” Loudoun County sheriff’s spokesperson Leah Paul told NBC News in a statement.

title: BTS Chooses Not to Submit to the Grammys After New Asian Pop Category Announced
summary: Why K-pop group BTS will not be submitting their music to next year’s Grammy Awards, the members announced July 28.
story: K-pop group BTS will not be submitting their music to next year’s Grammy Awards, the members announced July 28.
The group — made up of members RM, Jimin, V, Suga, Jungkook, Jin and J-Hope — shared the same statement on their individual Instagram stories.

The announcement comes just over a month after the Recording Academy — the body of musicians, producers, engineers and more that vote on the awards, announced five new categories — including a “Best Asian Pop Music Performance,” which would include K-pop among other genres.

“We have decided not to enter the Grammys this year,” reads a translation of the message, which was written in Korean. “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language.”

In a statement shared with TODAY.com, Grammys CEO Harvey Mason Jr. said that he was “saddened” to hear BTS’ decision, but understood and respected the choice. Mason also said that artists who submit to a genre category — such as Asian pop, jazz or country — are not excluded from also submitting to, and being considered in, the general field categories. These categories include record of the year, album of the year and song of the year.

“Those categories remain open to any eligible recording, regardless of genre,” Mason said in the statement. “Recognition in a genre category and recognition in the General Field are not mutually exclusive. An artist can absolutely pursue both.”
Mason also said that the Asian pop category was “created to celebrate the depth, diversity and extraordinary growth” of pop music out of Asia.
“More categories mean more artists’ work is recognized,” Mason said in the statement.

According to the Academy’s description of the new categories, which was announced on June 16, the best Asian pop music performance would recognize performances “originating from or widely recognized within Asian markets.” This would include K-pop, J-pop, C-pop and more, and involve the “meaningful use of one or more Asian languages.”

BTS, which stands for Bangtan Sonyeondan, or Bulletproof Boy Scouts, would have been able to submit work off of their newest album “Arirang,” which came out in March. The album marks the group’s first album together after each of the members completed their mandatory military service in Korea.

The group has a special spot in Grammys history. In 2019, they became the first K-pop act to present at the prestigious awards show. The group, which presented the best R&B album, had the honor of handing the award to winner H.E.R. for her self-titled album.
“Growing up in South Korea, we always dreamed of being on the Grammys stage,” said bandmember RM, according to Variety. “Thank you to all our fans for making this dream come true and we’ll be back.”

A year later, they became the first K-pop act to perform at the awards show, putting on a stunning performance alongside rapper Lil Nas X for the hit “Old Town Road.” And in 2022, they performed the hit single “Butter,” which has racked up more than 115 million views on YouTube alone.

They’ve also earned five Grammy award nominations, including three for best pop duo/group performance and one best music video nod for 2013’s “Yet to Come (The Most Beautiful Moment).” While they were the first K-pop group to receive any Grammy nods, they have yet to win an award.

Most recently, the group made headlines for their performance at the World Cup Finals halftime show on July 19. Dressed in black, white and red coordinating ensembles, BTS took over the pitch with an electrifying performance of their song “Dynamite.”

title: ‘Tony’ Reviews: Here’s What Critics Are Saying About the Anthony Bourdain Biopic
summary: Here’s what critics are saying about the Anthony Bourdain biopic, “Tony.”
story: Anthony Bourdain takes center stage in “Tony,” a biopic of the late chef and author.

In the film, Dominic Sessa, known for his work in the Academy Award-winning 2023 comedy-drama “The Holdovers,” as well as 2025’s “Now You See Me: Now You Don’t,” fills the role of a young, blunt Bourdain. The film, directed by Matt Johnson, also stars Antonio Banderas, Emilia Jones and Leo Woodall.
Bourdain died by suicide in 2018, yet the author — who wrote bestselling 2000 book “Kitchen Confidential,” which rocketed him to stardom — continues to inspire fans to this day.
“Tony” takes moviegoers back to a 19-year-old Bourdain in the summer of 1975, when he worked at a seafood restaurant in Cape Cod, Massachusetts.
The film, which has a 100% score on Rotten Tomatoes as of July 29, opens Aug. 7 and is poised to take a bite out of the box office.
Thinking of checking it out? Here’s what the critics are saying.
The Hollywood Reporter
“A slender slice of a famous life, the movie feels a little wispy in its mix of scrappy and sweet, rough-edged and yet bathed in the balming glow of nostalgia,” David Rooney writes.
“But it has an idiosyncratic charm that fits the title character, without ever sanding down the abrasive side of a chronic liar or masking his insecurities.”
Rooney also praised Sessa’s performance.

“Making good on his promise in ‘The Holdovers,’ Dominic Sessa is excellent in the role, nailing the contradictory aspects of a slippery character while mapping his coming-of-age arc with empathy and honesty,” he writes.
“There’s no dark foreshadowing of the tragedy we know will come 43 years later — only chutzpah, raw potential and intermittent flickers of vulnerability.”
The Daily Beast

Nick Schager’s review echoed the sentiment that Sessa holds his own in the film, noting it “becomes more convincing and authentic with each passing scene, it has a rough-around-the-edges charm that’s in keeping with its go-for-broke protagonist.”
Schager also cites the film’s “spontaneity and genuineness” and lauds Banderas’ work.

“‘Tony’ swings and sways like a lobster boat in choppy waters off the New England coast, and though that setting would seem to be an unlikely place to find Antonio Banderas, the star makes for a delightful boss and, eventually, mentor,” he writes.

Schager says “Tony” serves as a “prologue” for the success Bourdain would later find, calling it a “tad slight” when considering the rich life Bourdain eventually led. However, the film is successful when assessed in its own “limited terms.”
“It may be little more than a tease that leads viewers to Bourdain’s copious written and screen works, but as far as amuse-bouches go, ‘Tony’ is a memorably tasty one,” he writes.
Variety
Owen Gleiberman opens his review, pondering “what Bourdain himself would have made of the movie.”
“To me, if an Anthony Bourdain biopic can’t clear the bar called ‘Bourdain would have liked it,’ it’s probably not a good movie,” he continues. “‘Tony’ clears that bar.”
He also applauds Johnson’s directorial effort.

“‘Tony’ has been framed as the origin story of how Anthony Bourdain became Anthony Bourdain,” he writes. “But one of the many things that Matt Johnson ... understands is that Anthony — or, as he called himself then, Tony — already was Anthony Bourdain.”
Gleiberman said the film marks a watershed moment for Sessa.

“To me, one of the most pleasurable things in movies is that moment when you see an actor become a movie star,” he writes “That’s what happens to Dominic Sessa in ‘Tony.’ I don’t care if the film is a summer indie smash or not (though it deserves to be) — it shows you that Sessa has the goods.”
The Wrap
William Bibbiani’s review begins by comparing “Tony” to “The Social Network,” explaining how the biopic understands “how to really make us care about” a person who is not necessarily appealing.
“‘Tony’ never makes young Bourdain entirely likable,” he writes later.

“This isn’t a superhero origin story where he changes and becomes a do-gooder at the end,” he continues. “This is an origin story about Bourdain’s inciting incident, the exact moment in his life where he realized he needed to change. In Matt Johnson’s hands, that’s epic enough for a whole film.”
Still, the movie left him feeling somewhat hollow.

“By the time the credits roll, ‘Tony’ has long since receded in a formula,” he writes. “The big finale feels contrived and a little unconvincing. I guess the filmmakers thought subverting the tone of a biopic was enough, so Johnson throws Bourdain’s fan base a bone. It just doesn’t have any meat on it.”
The film, Bibbiani goes on to write, does however earn the viewer’s affection — “mostly because it never pretends Bourdain has.”

“We are invited to view the genius as a work in progress. Bourdain’s rough draft stinks; the film about this rough draft is polished and interesting, but another round of notes wouldn’t have killed it,” he writes. “We’re watching a guy who will one day reach his full potential, in a movie that doesn’t entirely reach its own.”
Associated Press
Mark Kennedy’s opening paragraph takes a big swing at a missed opportunity.
“Like all first courses, it leaves you with a nice first taste — but still hungry,” he writes.
Kennedy writes that the film’s director and co-writer Matt Johnson took “liberties with a formative period in Bourdain’s life.”
However, he “still only manages to tell the story of how a callow lad became somewhat of a less callow lad after toiling in a restaurant kitchen on Cape Cod in 1975,” Kennedy writes.
Kennedy laments how this picture could’ve been even better.
“In ‘Tony,’ the world-weary, forever romantic, noodle-slurping Bourdain that we would fall in love with decades later via travel shows like “Parts Unknown” stays firmly out of grasp,” he writes.
Kennedy also asks whether it was necessary to place Bourdain at the center of this film.
“Who doesn’t like a good coming of age?” Kennedy writes. “Why did it have to be Bourdain if Bourdain never gets to be Bourdain?”
ScreenRant
Matt Harrison credits the film, which he calls “laugh-out-loud funny” for making an entertaining flick with Bourdain as the central character.
“It works on its own terms, with or without the halo of its subject’s career. It’s actually about something. And it’s a delight to watch,” he writes.
“It’s sincerely interested in who this lost 19-year-old thinks he is, who he actually is, and who he’s going to choose to become,” he adds.

Harrison, who calls the film “thoroughly enjoyable,” also singled out how the scenes in the kitchen feel “truly alive.” And Sessa “can embody all the epigraph’s unlikable traits and remain remarkably easy to root for.”
IndieWire
“‘Tony’ retains the sincere flavor of street meat despite being factory-processed within an inch of its life,” David Ehrlich writes.
He also salutes Sessa’s “wholly self-possessed lead performance” and how Johnson framed one of the early and key parts of Bourdain’s journey.

“Johnson recognizes how this, at heart, is a coming-of-age story about a rising star who’s learning to be unburdened by a future that’s better than he could ever imagine — a kid who’s learning that no one can become the person they pretend to be without being the person they actually are along the way,” he writes.
“‘Tony’ struggles for an ending, but it doesn’t really need one; the real fun here lies in paving the way to parts unknown.”

title: The Nickname Robert Pattinson’s Daughter Has For ‘The Batman’ Star Is Too Cute
summary: Musician Suki Waterhouse said that her 2-year-old daughter, whom she shares with fiancé Robert Pattinson, isn’t really bothered by Pattinson’s slightly scary costume and makeup that he wears while playing Batman.
story: Musician Suki Waterhouse said that her 2-year-old daughter, whom she shares with fiancé Robert Pattinson, isn’t really bothered by Pattinson’s slightly scary costume and makeup that he wears while playing Batman.
In fact, it seems the toddler is embracing her dad’s alter-ego.
During an appearance on a recent episode of the “And The Writer Is” podcast, Waterhouse, 34, revealed the sweet nickname the toddler uses when she sees Pattinson, 40, as the vigilante.
“She calls him, like, ‘Daddy Batman’ now because he’s always dressed up like that for the next seven months whenever he’s on FaceTime,” said the singer, who gave birth to the baby girl in 2024.
During the podcast episode, Waterhouse opened up about being a mom, revealing how her daughter processes her parents’ unique jobs.
The couple have not publicly revealed their daughter’s name.

The songwriter told host fellow musician Ross Golan that her daughter understands that Waterhouse is a musician and that her dad dons a cape and mask to portray Batman. She shared the funny moment that she and her daughter had on FaceTime with Pattinson, who called them from the set of the long-anticipated “The Batman” sequel, “The Batman Part II,” which is currently in production.
“She’s on FaceTime to her dad who today is covered in blood with huge black circles around his eyes and I’m like, ‘Hi, is it fine?’ And we’re just like, ‘It’s fine,’” she told Golan.

While Pattinson is away filming, Waterhouse has been enjoying some mother-daughter bonding time. She shared on the podcast that she and her daughter were flipping through a book the other day, when the toddler spotted a girl holding a guitar.
“She was like, ‘That’s your job,’” she recalled to Golan.
Waterhouse said her daughter had been watching her play guitar and practice her set as she prepared for her “Loveland Tour,” which kicked off on July 22 in Phoenix, Arizona.
“She’ll say, like, ‘mommy songs’ (and) I’ll show her my music videos and stuff and so it’s cool,” she continued.
Waterhouse added that her daughter enjoys sitting in on glam sessions with her hair and makeup team and looking at the different nail polish options.
Waterhouse and Pattinson, who were first spotted together in 2018, have both opened up about their family and the experience of raising a daughter.
When Waterhouse stopped by TODAY in December 2024, she gushed that she was “completely and utterly besotted” with her baby girl.
“I didn’t know that it would be this good,” she said.
After her appearance, she spoke with TODAY.com and talked about how excited she was to be taking her daughter on tour for the first time.
She explained, “There’s so many hours before you get on stage of walking around, being in a different city — doing that with her will be amazing.”
Waterhouse also shared that her favorite moment of the day was playing in the pool with her daughter and fiancé.

“We have, like, a routine of putting her in the swimming pool and jumping in and out of the pool,” she said. “That’s just always the most fun, like, end of the day, 5 p.m., we all get in the pool and be silly. It’s amazing.”
Pattinson has also talked about parenthood, discussing how he has grown since becoming a father in an interview with Icon Magazine published in October 2025.
The proud dad said, “I have so much more patience. It’s funny, it’s not even patience; I genuinely enjoy hanging out with babies. That surprised me.”

He playfully added, “It’s also funny how you start having real, normie conversations — about things like schools or daycares… it’s so strange. It’s like, there’s this gravitational pull…Like, I have to wear Patagonia puffer jackets and cargo shorts now. I just have to.”

title: What Happens to Drew Starkey’s Character Cary in ‘Lucky’?
summary: Does Cary die in Lucky? What happens to Cary in Lucky? Here’s a recap of Episode 4 of the Apple TV series “Lucky”.
story: Warning: Spoilers ahead for “Lucky.”

“You’re alive. Good for you,” are the first words Lucky utters to her husband Cary after finding him hiding out in a luxurious beachside home while she has been fighting to survive ever since he left.

“Lucky,” the Apple TV miniseries based on Marissa Stapley’s novel of the same name starring Anya Taylor-Joy as the titular character, opened with the protagonist being abandoned by her husband, played by Drew Starkey, after the two stole $10 million and planned to run off together.

In the first three episodes of the crime thriller, Lucky is on the run, dodging the FBI and her mother-in-law Priscilla, (Annette Bening) who happens to be a crime boss. The con artist is looking for answers, too, as she tries to track down her deceitful spouse and figure out why he betrayed her.

Her answers arrive in Episode 4, out July 29, when Lucky and Cary come face-to-face for the first time. During an intense and bloody confrontation, Cary reveals why he left his wife confused and alone, and what happened to the money. His revelation leads to a heartbreaking scene at the end of the episode that sets up Lucky’s journey for the rest of the season.
Read on to find out where Cary has been and what happens to his character below.
Why Did Cary Leave Lucky?

When Cary walks into his hideout and finds his scorned wife waiting for him, he admits he knew she would track him down. He attempts to explain his actions and make amends. But she isn’t interested at first, instead punching him in the face after he approaches her.

Lucky berates him for leaving her scared and vulnerable and accuses him of never loving her. He apologizes and assures her their relationship is real. He reveals that he left because his mom planned to kill Lucky.

We learn in a flashback scene that Cary previously visited his mom and she shared that she knew Lucky had stolen millions from her. Priscilla also learned that Lucky had turned her in to the FBI, sending her to prison for years. Cary calls Lucky out for keeping that secret from him throughout their marriage.

Despite feeling hurt, Cary still wanted to protect his wife. So, he drugged her after their night out in Las Vegas, took the money and left their hotel room in the wee hours of the morning. When he reached his mom, he changed his mind and decided to return to Lucky. But when he arrived at the hotel, he saw the building was surrounded by police and drove away.
Cary took the money and deposited most of it into a Bitcoin account, protected by a seed phrase. He used the rest of the money to purchase his secret spot in La Jolla, California.

When Lucky asks for the phrase and he refuses, she threatens to shoot him. Before she can pull the trigger, the FBI, led by Agent Billie Rand (Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor), bang on the door and demand Cary come outside.
Does Lucky Forgive Cary?
As the FBI enter, Lucky and Cary flee in their getaway car.

A high-speed hunt ensues through the streets of San Diego. Just when Cary and Lucky think they have evaded the authorities, they run into Priscilla, who also starts chasing them. Then, the police are on their trail again.
Possibly facing death, Lucky confesses to her husband that she still loves him. “I don’t regret us,” she tells him.
“Neither do I,” he replies.
Does Cary Die?
Unfortunately, yes.

Cary decides to slow down the police by leaning out the window and attempting to shoot the tires of the cop cars. He and the police exchange fire. When one of the tires on Cary and Lucky’s car is shot, the vehicle flips over multiple times.
Lucky awakes and sees that while Cary survived the crash, he was shot by one of the officers. She tries to stop the bleeding and keep him alive, but it doesn’t work.
“You were happy…” he tells her before his eyes close and he dies.
What Will Happen in Episode 5?
With no time to mourn the death of her husband, Lucky sneaks out of the vehicle and goes on the run once more.

With only three episodes remaining, including the finale out on Aug. 19, viewers will see if Lucky will manage to stay alive and how she will retrieve the money now that Cary died without sharing the seed phrase.
Plus, viewers will likely watch Lucky and Priscilla face off and see how she’ll get help from her dad John (Timothy Olyphant) despite him being in prison.
Episode 5, titled “Are We Bad People?” will be released on Aug. 5.

title: Fabien Frankel Talks Shocking ‘House of the Dragon’ Twist: ‘I Knew I Had it Coming’
summary: Fabien Frankel talks his character Criston Cole meeting his bloody demise in “The Butcher’s Ball” on TODAY.
story: Warning: This post contains spoilers for “House of the Dragon.”
Fabien Frankel’s Criston Cole fulfilled his wish of dying “the realm’s greatest warrior” when met his bloody demise in “House of the Dragon.”
Minutes into Season 3, Episode 6 of “House of the Dragon,” entitled “The Butcher’s Ball,” Ser Cole led his men onto a battlefield that he thought was filled with deceased soldiers.

But his enemies were simply tricking him and arose, launching a sudden attack. Although Cole begged for his life and tried to surrender, his pleas were ignored and he died after being hit by multiple arrows.

It was an honorable death for Cole, and one he didn’t fear. In the episode prior, he said in a monologue, “I have been a servant all my life, to Green or to Black. I have defined myself by oaths, through unyielding devotion. And the highborn have made much of me while it pleased them to do so. But I will not let them diminish me now. I will not return spurned, rejected. I am the realm’s greatest warrior. And I will die as such.”
During an appearance on TODAY July 29, Frankel opened up about his character’s death.

“I knew I had it coming. I’d done so much bad stuff. I knew at some point I’d get a call saying our time was up. I lived a life. I did a lot of episodes. It was a good, long journey,” Frankel said on TODAY.
Frankel said he would “do a bit” with his friends about coming back for the show’s next season, even though his character’s fate was clearly spelled out in the book that inspired the show.

“I kept doing a while bit where I’d say, ‘I gotta go back next year, do a whole new season of the show.’ My friends were like, ‘You’re really lying directly to my face,’” he said. “I feel that’s apt for Criston and apt for myself.”
Frankel also described the “outpouring” he’s witnessed since his character’s death.
“There’s more love for Criston now than I felt ... now that he’s not alive, people maybe feel a little bit worse about hating him so much,” he said with a smile.
Cole, a divisive character, had appeared on the fantasy series since it premiered in 2022.

A day after the death of his character aired, Frankel posted a tribute to Cole on Instagram. Beside a carousel of behind-the-scenes photos taken on the set of the HBO series, Frankel wrote in the caption, “3 seasons. 21 episodes. 5 and half years. A badly dealt with heartbreak.”
He added, “To all of you who tuned in every week, And to all those who have carried me along the way, I couldn’t have gotten through it without you. It’s been an honour. Criston Cole, over and out.”
Fans complimented Frankel’s performance on the show in the comments.
“Hated your character which means you are a spectacular actor sir,” one said.
Another agreed and wrote, “A sign of a great actor is that they can make you hate them on screen. You were up there with some of the most hated in the GoT universe and we love you for that!”
The official HBO account also left a message that read, “We thank you for your valiant service to the crown, Ser Fabien.”

title: Oscar-Winning Irish Singer-Songwriter Glen Hansard Dies in Dublin Motorcycle Crash
summary: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin early Wednesday, his management said.
story: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin early Wednesday, his management said. He was 56.
ATC Management told broadcaster RTE Hansard’s family was “deeply shocked and heartbroken” by his death.

Irish police said a man in his 50s died in single vehicle motorcycle crash in Lucan on the outskirts of the Irish capital before 4:30 a.m. on Wednesday. The man, who they did not name, was treated at the scene but was pronounced dead a short time later.

Hansard combined acting and a musical career. He played a member of a Dublin soul band in 1991 movie “The Commitments” and won an Oscar in 2008 for the song “Falling Slowly” from the film “Once,” in which he starred alongside Markéta Irglová.

He was long-serving front man for rock band The Frames, half of rock duo The Swell Season and released solo albums including “Didn’t He Ramble,” which was nominated for a Grammy for Best Folk Album in 2016.
For years, Hansard led the Christmas Eve charity busk outside Dublin’s Gaiety Theatre, where members of the public gathered to see famous Irish musicians perform in aid of the Dublin Simon Community.

At the funeral of The Pogues frontman Shane MacGowan in 2023, Hansard performed The Pogues’ song “Fairytale Of New York” with Irish singer Lisa O’Neill, which prompted dancing in the aisles of the church.
Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin said he was “deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Glen Hansard.”
“A talented musician and actor who made a significant contribution to Ireland’s cultural landscape over many years,” Martin posted on X.

title: Karlie Kloss Calls Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce an ‘Amazing Couple’ After Going to Their Wedding: EXCLUSIVE
summary: Karlie Kloss opened up to TODAY about her new book and said that Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are an “amazing couple.’
story: Weeks after being photographed heading to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in New York, Karlie Kloss opened up about the nuptials.

“Listen, I try to protect the privacy of my friends’ personal lives,” Kloss said during an appearance on TODAY on July 28. “But what I will say is that they’re an amazing couple and I’m so happy for them.”

Swift and Kelce’s wedding unfolded on July 3 in New York, drawing a star-studded crowd to Madison Square Garden. While most of the wedding has been kept secret, guests have shared a few details, like handkerchiefs embroidered with a T&T logo and who, exactly, caught the bouquet.

Kloss and Swift met at a fashion show in 2013, Swift confirmed to Vogue in 2015, and became fast friends. The two shared bits of their friendship with the world and the press. Kloss even appeared in Swift’s “Bad Blood” music video in 2015.

However, the two have not been photographed or seen together publicly since 2016. Swift did not attend either of Kloss’ wedding ceremonies to Joshua Kushner in 2018 and 2019. Of their friendship, a 2018 New York Times profile of Kloss said, “Despite internet gossip suggesting otherwise, the pair continues to be good friends and they talk frequently.”

Kloss, meanwhile, is interested in untangling a different type of problem. Over a decade ago, the former supermodel started a non-profit technology education program, Kode With Klossy, a camp that connects young girls with opportunities and support in the technology and computer science space.
Her first children’s book, “Spaghetti Code: A Story About Problem-Solving, Pasta, and the Power of Big Ideas,” out July 28, introduces coding concepts to 4 to 8-year-olds.

“‘Spaghetti code’ is a term that means when your code is a hot mess. There’s a bug in there somewhere and you’ve got to fix it,” Kloss said on TODAY. “The idea is to not get frustrated or overwhelmed when you hit a mistake, but to work through it and keep going.”
The mom of three called her leap into writing a children’s picture book about coding principles a “tall order,” but wanted it to be “really fun and visual.”
“‘Spaghetti Code’ is really inspired by our scholars, who are these incredible, passionate young women from around the world,” Kloss said.
“Spaghetti Code” is the first in a five-book series, per Publisher’s Weekly.

title: John Mulaney Announces 9 New York City Shows: EXCLUSIVE
summary: John Mulaney has revealed he will perform at nine New York City venues over nine straight days, ending with a performance at Madison Square Garden.
story: He’s already conquered the Windy City — now John Mulaney has his eyes set on the Big Apple.

Mulaney, who became the first comedian to headline Chicago’s Wrigley Field during a July 11 show, has announced “Mulaney Takes Manhattan,” a series of nine shows over nine days in New York City, culminating with a performance at Madison Square Garden, he revealed exclusively on TODAY on July 28.

“Instead of doing one show in New York City, or even three shows in New York City, for my tour, I’m going to do a very special run. Nine different iconic New York City venues in nine nights,” he said.

“This is very, very cool, I must say. I’m doing something very cool, and I’m a very cool person,” he joked. “This is really a great way to do the intimate small places. I love playing here, building up to Madison Square Garden, doing Radio City (Music Hall). I filmed a special at Radio City, to go back there. It’s going to be really cool.”
The shows, which will begin Jan. 7, 2027 and end Jan. 15, 2027, will feature special guests and a new experience each performance.
You can sign up for a chance to get tickets at johnmulaney.com.
Here’s a look at all of the shows.

Mulaney is in the middle of his “Mister Whatever Tour,” which stopped at Wrigley Field — home of the Chicago Cubs — for his history-making performance.
“It was iconic. It might’ve been too big,” he said.
“It was like playing a spaceship. And who brought me up, but Mr. David Letterman,” he added, as video of the legendary comedian introducing him played, a moment that left him in awe.
“What’s cool about something that crazy is you don’t even have to put it in perspective. It was just wild. And then the show itself was like flying a spaceship,” he said.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Ends With Surprising Elimination After Contestant Gets Injured
summary: Another contestant has been eliminated on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” The third episode saw one dancer leave the ballroom after group challeneges.
story: There’s no room for mistakes as the competition continues on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.”
With nine dancers remaining, Episode 3 of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff is challenging the contestants with group performances.

“DWTS” pro Britt Stewart joined judges Shirley and Mark Ballas during the Monday, July 27, episode. The dancer helped mentor the contestants as they took on high-intensity routines that they had to learn and master in just hours.
Group performances are key to opening a “DWTS” live show and entertaining the audiences. They also test the individuals on teamwork, taking direction, giving feedback and timing.
So, how did the contestants fare?
What Happened During Episode 3 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’
Britt entered the ballroom performing a dynamic group tango that impressed all. Host Robert Irwin then revealed that the dancers’ first challenge would be to re-create Britt’s exact choreography.

Then it was time for rehearsals, where the nine contestants learned the steps and took direction from Britt. Some felt they excelled in group performances, while others faced difficulties being in sync, spacing and picking up the choreography.

However, in one unexpected moment Natalie Jolley was accidentally hit in the eye by Stephani Sosa. Natalie was transported to the hospital to receive medical attention, which meant the group was down by one.

The show had to continue and after just three hours of rehearsals, Britt informed the crew that it was time to perform for the judges. She said that was the amount of time “DWTS” pros had to learn opening numbers and be camera ready.

The performance had its hits and misses, with the judges determining that Tristan Sanders and Nina Mayster were the weakest links. But, they were not on the chopping block just yet. Britt informed them that they would have another chance to prove their skills in the second group challenge.

Given a chance to redeem themselves, Tristan, who became emotional following feedback, and Nina were then chosen to be the team captains in the second challenge. The two had to select who they wanted on their teams to create and perform another group dance. Meanwhile, Natalie was under “medical supervision” and could not participate.
On Nina’s team were Allen Genkin, AJ Pritchard and Adele Zaikman. They had to perform a tango.
Tristan chose Stephani, Selena Hamilton and Erik Linder. They would be performing a paso doble.
